In the cases where exact diagonalization is possible, the eigenspace of lowest eigenvalue is one- or two-dimensional, and the eigenvalue, as well as the structure of the eigenstates depends on the cutoff. These ground states are entangled across the three edges. The variational method does not find the lowest eigenspace, but near kernel states, i.e., states with components in a number of low lying eigenspaces. For low cutoffs, they also do not factorize across the three edge degrees of freedom. At larger cutoffs, it increasingly finds near kernel states that factorize over the edges, matched with near-unit fidelity by reduced Thiemann coherent states. We discuss some indication that these states are the optimal near-kernel states if factorization is assumed.

items.title: Next-Generation Segmentation in Radiotherapy: A Narrative Review from Atlas-Based Methods to Agentic Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Precise segmentation of target volumes and organs at risk is an essential prerequisite for modern, high-precision radiation therapy. However, this task has traditionally been time-consuming and subject to high interobserver variability. Motivated by these limitations, more advanced and novel approaches to automating this task have been developed over the past two decades. This narrative review highlights representative milestones, with a focus on the most recent developments. These approaches include atlas-based label propagation, convolutional architectures, promptable foundation models, and, most recently, vision-language models (VLMs), which integrate clinical text with volumetric segmentation. Each methodological generation has addressed limitations of its predecessor while introducing new ones. A substantial gap remains between research progress and clinical deployment, as routine workflows continue to be dominated by atlas-based and narrow task-specific deep-learning tools, which remain strong baselines in geometric overlap metrics but are highly rigid in terms of application, versatility, portability, and interpretability. As contouring systems further grow in complexity, conventional geometric overlap metrics become insufficient, motivating evaluation paradigms that incorporate surface-based, dosimetric, and prompt-adherence assessment. Emerging agentic architectures that combine large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, and vision-language segmentation modules are leading towards more flexible, guideline-aware, interactive contouring workflows. These systems could automate flexible and interpretable knowledge-based contouring and actively support the clinical reasoning underlying target volume definition.

items.title: Global MHD simulations of the solar convective zone using a volleyball mesh decomposition. I. Pilot
items.summary: Solar modelling has long been split into `internal' and `surface' modelling because of the lack of tools to connect the very different scales in space and time, as well as the widely different environments and the dominating physical effects involved. Significant efforts have recently been put into resolving this disconnect. We address the outstanding bottlenecks in connecting internal convection zone and dynamo simulations to the surface of the Sun, and conduct a proof-of-concept high-resolution global simulation of the convection zone of the Sun, using the task-based DISPATCH code framework. We present a new `volleyball' mesh decomposition, which has Cartesian patches tessellated on a sphere with no singularities. We use our new entropy based HLLS approximate Riemann solver to model magneto-hydrodynamics in a global simulation, ranging between 0.655---0.998 R$_\odot$, with an initial ambient magnetic field set to 0.1 Gauss. This paper describes the methods and the pilot runs of the setup. The mesh decomposition exhibits neither unwanted artefacts, nor noise build-up. The simulations develop convective motions with complex, turbulent structures. Small-scale dynamo action twists the ambient magnetic field and locally amplifies magnetic field magnitudes by more than two orders of magnitude within the initial run-time.

items.title: Numerical quality factor statistics for superconducting rf cavities with spatially inhomogeneous multilayer coatings modeled by Gaussian random fields
items.summary: Bulk niobium has long been the material of choice for superconducting radio-frequency applications. An alternative approach is the superconductor-insulator-superconductor multilayer structure, which enables the use of brittle high-$T_c$ materials such as NbTiN. At present, SIS coatings are limited to flat samples, with the single-cell TESLA cavity representing a key milestone. Extending coating processes to non-flat geometries is expected to introduce macroscopic inhomogeneities in coating thickness. We model these variations using Gaussian random fields parametrized by a length scale, and generated by solving a stochastic partial differential equation. The resulting field is incorporated into the boundary condition of the cavity eigenvalue problem, from which quantities of interest -- such as resonant frequency and quality factor -- are computed. This procedure is repeated for eight length scales, with \num{2048} samples per length scale, where the resulting quality factors are recorded. Our results show that the quality factors follow a normal distribution. The standard deviation increases with the length scale and can be statistically distinguished. In contrast, the mean values remain largely unchanged, with only a few significant differences. In extreme cases, depending on the length scale, the quality factor may differ from the uniform case by \SIrange{2}{6}{\percent}.

items.title: Repeated Binary Direct Collinear Impacts Under Incremental Contact Laws With Residual Indentation: A Hybrid Systems Formulation
items.summary: Incremental contact laws specify the normal contact force through a differential relation, possibly carrying an internal state, driven by the indentation and its rate. The force may vanish at a nonzero indentation, through plasticity, an elastic aftereffect, or, under some laws with a viscous component, a load drawing the bodies apart rapidly, leaving a residual deformation at separation. Such a deformation sits uneasily within rigid body dynamics, which admits none. The tension is tolerable when the indentation is small relative to the bodies, so that it may be carried constitutively rather than geometrically. Even then, the law alone does not determine the interaction: because force and indentation no longer vanish together, conditions for the commencement and termination of contact must be supplied separately, as must the fate of the deformation and internal state at separation, both absent from the equations of motion. This article formulates the repeated direct collinear impact of two convex bodies under external forces as a hybrid dynamical system. The contact interface is modeled as a massless element carrying the contact law and its state, coupled to the bodies through relative velocity and an interaction force dictated by the contact state. Consequently, all switching and resets are confined to the interface, leaving the geometry and equations of motion of the bodies unaltered. The principal analytical properties of the formulations are established, among them passivity and completeness; the branching of solutions at the onset and termination of contact is examined. The framework is demonstrated through numerical simulations.

items.title: A Self-Consistent Two-Carrier Drift-Diffusion Framework for p-n Junctions: Extended Diode Equation, Power Dissipation, and Base Transit Time
items.summary: The classical theory of p-n junctions derives the current-voltage characteristic from minority-carrier diffusion alone: majority carriers are treated as an inert background, the quasi-neutral base as field-free, and the junction voltage as equal to the applied bias. These premises fail together under high bias and high-level injection, where the observed current roll-off is reproduced only by appending an empirical series resistance outside the junction physics. Here we develop a self-consistent two-carrier drift-diffusion framework that introduces no assumption beyond the classical ones. Excess majority carriers are shown to be electrostatically forced transport participants: the ambipolar diffusion equation, closed by exact two-sided boundary conditions, yields a unified excess-carrier profile. The resulting base field separates into an ohmic and a Dember component, and all four current components follow in closed form, their sum being position independent. At device level the framework closes into an extended diode equation that contains the Shockley equation as its low-injection, long-base limit and reproduces the n=2 roll-off intrinsically. The junction voltage emerges as a self-limiting drop confined to the space-charge region and separated from the applied bias by exact base drops. Two device-level corrections are quantified: at high current, 75-90% of the dissipation migrates from the junction into the quasi-neutral base, and field-assisted acceleration shortens the base transit time by up to a factor of six. Three parameter-free predictions follow: a universal ideality-factor crossover that passes through 3/2 when the boundary excess equals the doping, a high-injection onset voltage that scales as 119 mV per decade of doping, and a geometry factor that survives into high injection.

items.title: The Extended Diode Equation
items.summary: For more than seven decades, the p-n junction current-voltage characteristic has been derived by treating majority carriers as an inert background and conflating the junction voltage with the applied bias. Here we show that the base electric field, generated by the coupling of excess majority and minority carriers, fundamentally alters the internal potential distribution. This self-consistent framework yields a closed-form extended diode equation that reproduces the high-injection roll-off without invoking an external series resistance, thereby eliminating an empirical patch that has persisted in the classical theory.

items.title: Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning for Microseismic Phase Picking Using a Neural Operator
items.summary: Seismic phase picking is fundamental for microseismic monitoring and subsurface imaging. Manual processing is impractical for real-time applications and large sensor arrays, motivating the use of deep learning-based pickers trained on extensive earthquake catalogs. On a broader scale, these models are generally tuned to perform optimally in high signal-to-noise and long-duration networks and often fail to perform satisfactorily when applied to campaign-based microseismic datasets, which are characterized by low signal-to-noise ratios, sparse geometries, and limited labeled data. In this study, we present a microseismic adaptation of a network-wide earthquake phase picker, Phase Neural Operator (PhaseNO), using transfer learning and parameter-efficient fine-tuning. Starting from a model pre-trained on more than 57,000 three-component earthquake and noise records, we fine-tune it using only 200 labeled and noisy microseismic recordings from hydraulic fracturing settings. We present a parameter-efficient adaptation of PhaseNO that fine-tunes a small fraction of its parameters (only 3.6%) while retaining its global spatiotemporal representations learned from a large dataset of earthquake recordings. We then evaluate our adapted model on three independent microseismic datasets and compare its performance against the original pre-trained PhaseNO, a STA/LTA-based workflow, and two state-of-the-art deep learning models, PhaseNet and EQTransformer. We demonstrate that our adapted model significantly outperforms the original PhaseNO in F1 and accuracy metrics, achieving up to 30% absolute improvements in all test sets and consistently performing better than STA/LTA and state-of-the-art models. With our adaptation being based on a small calibration set, our proposed workflow is a practical and efficient tool to deploy network-wide models in data-limited microseismic applications.

items.title: Variational principles for dissipative continua: transport theorems, inertia, and the minimum-maximum duality
items.summary: Variational principles for dissipative processes come in two families: minimum principles at nonequilibrium stationary states (Helmholtz, Kirchhoff, Prigogine) and maximum principles for relaxation in continuum mechanics (Ziegler, Hackl, Fischer). We contribute to the understanding of the thermodynamic extremal principle (TEP) by investigating its extremal properties, and uncover the connection between the two families, whose distinction was recently made precise for diffusion: the extremal character is decided by the regime, which is either relaxation at frozen state, as in a closed system (maximum dissipation), or a driven stationary state in an open system (minimum dissipation), while the underlying Rayleighian functional is convex and minimized in both cases. We further examine the Reynolds transport theorem, a useful tool for fixing the energy rates of continua, and the role of inertia, recently argued to lie beyond the reach of Rayleighian principles. With inertia the driving force must be held fixed during the variation, which is less elegant than in the inertialess case, where it is a state function. Writing the energy rate as rates times driving forces still yields the correct equations, and an extremal statement survives whenever the frozen force does not depend on the varied rate. This holds directly for unsteady Stokes flow, and for Navier-Stokes flow after a change to material coordinates, in which the particle acceleration is the second time derivative of the state and the convective term, nonvariational in the Eulerian description, does not appear. The framework is tested on the Navier-Stokes family (Stokes, unsteady Stokes, and Navier-Stokes flow, in order of increasing complexity) and on dissipative Lagrangian mechanics.

items.title: Leveraging High-Activity Post-Therapeutic I-131 Scans for Deep Learning Reconstruction of Extremely Sparse Planar Images in Differentiated Thyroid Cancer
items.summary: Background: Diagnostic I-131 whole-body planar imaging in differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC) is count-limited by low administered activity, and quality worsens under rapid acquisition. Models trained on such data struggle because their targets lack photon statistics. Purpose: To test whether high-quality post-therapeutic (PT) I-131 scans can serve as superior training references for enhancing sparse diagnostic planar images, using transfer learning and input-image addition. Methods: In this single-center prospective study, 111 patients were enrolled in PT training (n = 19), diagnostic follow-up (FU) training (n = 58), and FU paired test (n = 34) cohorts. Five Restormer-based models were trained: FU_DLx2 on FU labels; PT_DLx2 transfer-learned on PT data; PT_DLx1+ and PT_DLx2+ with input-image addition; PT_DLx6 as a PT-only reference. Test-time processing used two-step denormalization and Poisson re-scaling to preserve noise statistics. Quality was assessed by PSNR, SSIM, and a blinded dual-reader evaluation of all 34 test-cohort patients. Results: PT_DLx2 achieved the highest PSNR (34.4 +/- 3.6 dB) and SSIM (0.81 +/- 0.07). PT_DLx1+ and PT_DLx2+ were comparable (33.8 and 33.3 dB; SSIM 0.80). FU_DLx2 ranked below the unprocessed fast scan (30.3 vs. 32.0 dB; 0.76 vs. 0.79). Subjectively, PT_DLx2+ scored highest in image quality (4.54 +/- 0.60) and diagnostic confidence (4.54 +/- 0.60), surpassing the reference standard (4.19 +/- 0.83 and 4.31 +/- 0.81; P = 0.005 and P = 0.008). FU_DLx2 and PT_DLx6 scored lowest. Conclusion: Count-rich PT scans provide effective training priors for reconstructing extremely sparse images. Input-image addition and cross-domain transfer learning from PT data outperformed direct training on count-limited diagnostic data, supporting 2x scan acceleration with quality matching or exceeding the unaccelerated standard scan for selected PT-derived configurations.

items.title: New approach to approximate analytical solutions for a harmonic oscillator subject to combined linear and nonlinear damping
items.summary: We introduce a new approach to deriving approximate analytical solutions of a harmonic oscillator damped by purely nonlinear, or combinations of linear and nonlinear damping forces. Our approach is based on choosing a suitable trial solution, i.e. an ansatz, which is the product of the time-dependent amplitude and the oscillatory (trigonometric) function with a reduced frequency (due solely to linear damping) and an initial phase shift (due to both linear and nonlinear damping) compared to the undamped case. We derive the amplitude decay equation using the connection of the energy dissipation rate with the power of the total damping force. By matching our ansatz to the initial conditions, we obtain equations for its initial amplitude and initial phase. We demonstrate the validity of our approach for quadratic damping, a combination of linear and quadratic damping, and finally a combination of linear, quadratic, and Coulomb damping. For pure quadratic damping and for a combination of linear and quadratic damping, we compare our approximate analytical solutions with the corresponding numerical solutions and find that they describe the oscillator dynamics well in the regime of weak to moderately strong damping. For the combination of all three types of damping, our solutions agree well with the numerical solutions until the last half-period or the last few half-periods of the motion (primarily depending on the strength of the Coulomb damping). In addition, we show how to use our solutions to determine damping constants from given displacement vs. time data, demonstrating that they can be applied to the analysis of experiments.

items.title: Meteosat Third Generation imagery improves CNN-based SSI retrieval
items.summary: Accurate Surface Solar Irradiance (SSI) estimation is increasingly important for photovoltaic energy monitoring and forecasting. The recently introduced Meteosat Third Generation (MTG) satellite constellation provides imaging data with higher spatial resolution compared to the Meteosat Second Generation (MSG) satellite constellation, but its benefits for machine-learning-based SSI retrieval are not well established. We compare multi-resolution convolutional neural network models for 10-minute SSI retrieval over Northern Europe (Estonia) using either MSG/SEVIRI or MTG/FCI satellite imagery. We evaluate model performance against ground-based pyranometer measurements from eight Estonian meteorological stations using site-based cross-validation with a temporally independent test year and multiple training seeds. Model performance is also compared with the SARAH-3 physics-based satellite SSI product. The FCI-only model significantly outperformed the SEVIRI-only model under overcast and cloudy conditions, reducing RMSE by 5.1 W/m^2 and 6.5 W/m^2, respectively. However, under partly cloudy or clear skies, there was no statistically significant difference in RMSE between the FCI-only and the SEVIRI-only models. In all-sky conditions, the RMSE of the FCI-only model was 5.1 W/m^2 lower on average, but this difference was not statistically significant after Bonferroni correction. Compared with physics-based SARAH-3, the FCI-only model yielded skill scores of 28% under overcast conditions, 19% under cloudy conditions, and 17% overall. Furthermore, both models underperformed SARAH-3 in clear-sky conditions. These results show that higher-resolution MTG/FCI imagery improves CNN-based SSI retrieval when clouds dominate irradiance variability, but also indicate that higher resolution alone is insufficient to address clear-sky limitations in machine-learning-based SSI retrieval.

items.title: Split-Ring Couplers for On-Skin Wi-Fi Communication via an SSPP Waveguide Textile
items.summary: Textile spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP) waveguides offer guided on-body links, but their body-facing ground conductors obstruct coupling from on-skin wireless nodes. This letter presents a split-ring coupling interface using local ground recesses at the textile terminations, without patterned garment-side launchers. The capacitively loaded rings are supported by polydimethylsiloxane carriers with a thickness of 2~mm. An image-current model and full-wave simulations examine the effect of backing-ground spacing and determine the recess geometry. For a 450~mm textile waveguide on a water-filled body phantom, the measured $S_{21}$ at 2.45 GHz was $-$18.8~dB, versus $-$60.9~dB without the textile. A 625-position scan showed a maximum 5.1 dB reduction relative to the nominal position within the measured joint $\pm$5~mm placement region. A separate two-node IEEE~802.11n test demonstrated a 65~Mb/s physical-layer (PHY) rate with zero packet errors among 300 frames at $-$20~dBm transmit power through the coupler link. These results establish high-rate, placement-tolerant on-skin Wi-Fi communication through an SSPP waveguide textile.

items.title: Aircraft speed and height from Doppler-shifted sound and flight-track data
items.summary: The changing pitch of a passing aircraft is a familiar example of the Doppler effect. We use audio recordings of 40 aircraft passages to estimate the speed and height by two methods based on the Doppler effect. The endpoint method is an analytical model that uses the limiting frequencies at the start and end of each recording and the slope near the middle of the frequency-time curve. The second method fits the whole curve. Results from both methods are compared with independent flight-tracking data. The endpoint method consistently underestimates speed and height because the recorded frequencies have not approached their limiting values. The full curve fit agrees with the tracking data within about 3% in speed and 12% in height for steady passages, with poorer agreement when speed or height changes. Software developed with AI assistance made it practical to analyze this many passages. The comparison offers undergraduate students an example of testing model assumptions and identifying systematic errors in real measurements.

items.title: Parametric spatio-temporal reduced-order modelling via Spectral Proper Orthogonal Decomposition and Gaussian Process Regression
items.summary: We present SPOD-GPR, a non-intrusive, parametric, spatio-temporal reduced-order model (ROM) that combines Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD), Spectral POD (SPOD), and Gaussian Process Regression (GPR). A parametric POD first projects the high-dimensional state onto a low-dimensional subspace. The reduced trajectories are then divided into windowed sections, transformed into the frequency domain, and truncated to the most energetic frequencies. SPOD is then performed independently at each retained frequency, yielding temporally coherent modes and coefficients. The parametric dependence of the POD and SPOD bases is modelled by GPR on a local chart of the Grassmann manifold after Procrustes alignment. The SPOD modal coefficients are learned both as explicit functions of the parameters and through a parameter-conditioned autoregressive model that allows for temporal extrapolation beyond the training window. Gaussian processes are sampled jointly and pathwise via Matheron conditioning, ensuring that each predictive realization carries uncertainty quantification consistent with the posterior distribution. The method is tested on four parametric examples where the parameter values and the prediction horizon lie outside the training data: the two-dimensional anisotropic Kuramoto--Sivashinsky equation in a time-periodic and a travelling-wave regime, each parametrised by one of its two coefficients; flow past a cylinder parametrised by the Reynolds number; and flow past an elliptic obstacle parametrised by its semi-axes. In all cases, SPOD-GPR reduces the normalised mean absolute error compared to a POD-GPR baseline, and improves the calibration of the predictive uncertainty, especially in the fluid flow cases, where POD-GPR is severely overconfident. This opens the way to spectral, uncertainty-aware reduced-order models for many-query and real-time applications, such as digital twins.

items.title: Generative deep learning improves reconstruction of global historical climate records
items.summary: Instrumental observations from the early twentieth century are sparse and uncertain, limiting estimates of historical climate variability and change. Existing reconstructions rely largely on statistical interpolation, smoothing spatiotemporal variability and leading to underestimation of local extremes. Recent deterministic machine-learning approaches focus primarily on spatial inpainting of coarse-resolution temperature fields but do not explicitly quantify uncertainty or enforce spatiotemporal consistency. Here, we present GenCRest, a generative deep-learning model that reconstructs globally complete temperature and precipitation fields from sparse, uncertain observations using a generative prior learned from Earth-system models and reanalyses. GenCRest preserves accuracy, temporal persistence, and higher-order variability of climate dynamics, consistently outperforming statistical and machine-learning benchmarks. Applying GenCRest to observational records that underpin climate assessments, we find stronger early-twentieth-century ENSO variability and identify approximately 50% more El Niño events documented in the literature, which are not represented in established datasets. Our reconstructions reveal a more spatially heterogeneous history of temperature change during 1900--1980, with pronounced regional warming and cooling contrasts, particularly in the Arctic. For 1981--2024, our results suggest that recent assessments overestimate Arctic-mean warming due to interpolation smoothing, while underestimating warming in the Greenland, Barents, and Kara Seas. Furthermore, based on our seamless global reconstruction that infers precipitation variability across the oceans and under-monitored regions, we identify more widespread wet extremes over land in the early twentieth century and intensified regional wetting and drying across land and ocean in recent decades.

items.title: Extending the reach of real-space real-time TDDFT: new developments in the Octopus code
items.summary: Octopus is an open-source package implementing time-dependent density functional theory in a real-space, real-time formulation. Here we report on the developments since our previous contribution to the Special Topic Issue on Electronic Structure Software [J. Chem. Phys. 152, 124119 (2020)]. New exchange-correlation functionals extend the range of systems that can be treated, while advances in relativistic and all-electron methods open the door to core-electron spectroscopy. New capabilities for lattice dynamics - stress-tensor calculation, geometry optimization, support for machine-learned force fields, and phonon calculations - enable a fully ab initio description of light-induced lattice dynamics in real time. We also present developments that move beyond the dipole approximation, capturing light-matter interaction more faithfully. Improved methods for exciton dynamics complement a set of algorithmic advances - new propagation schemes, imaginary-time evolution, and a refactored grid handling more than a billion points - that together substantially improve performance and scalability. Combined with technical improvements such as AMD GPU support and a modernized build system, these developments consolidate Octopus as a versatile, high-performance platform for exploring electronic excitations, light-matter interaction, and nonequilibrium dynamics in molecules, nanostructures, and extended systems.

items.title: Scalable Bayesian Optimization for Efficient Exploration of Moire Patterns
items.summary: Large materials design spaces often contain rare high-performing configurations that are difficult to identify through trial-and-error exploration or purely representative machine-learning (ML) sampling. In this work, we present FruBO, a flexible Bayesian Optimization framework for accelerating the discovery of optimal configurations in computationally demanding materials design problems. As a case study, we investigate multilayer Moiré patterns generated by the superposition of six rotated hexagonal lattices, where the objective is to identify the rotational conformation that maximizes pore-size uniformity, quantified using the Jain fairness index. The resulting benchmark contains 600,000 unique configurations and exhibits a highly skewed objective distribution, making the global optimum difficult to locate by random sampling. We compare random exploration, Gaussian Process-based Bayesian Optimization, and Bayesian Optimization using a lightweight CatBoost surrogate with committee-based uncertainty estimation. Random sampling identifies the global optimum only after 533,012 evaluations, requiring approximately 31 hours, while Gaussian Process-based BO becomes impractical due to GPU memory exhaustion after 290 acquired samples. In contrast, FruBO with CatBoost identifies the global optimum after 1,470 acquired samples and approximately 1.15 hours. These results demonstrate that scalable surrogate models can substantially improve the feasibility and efficiency of BO in large nanomaterials design spaces.

items.title: Phase-resolved turbulence dynamics in cardiac-cycle-inspired pulsatile pipe flow
items.summary: Direct numerical simulations examine the phase-dependent turbulence dynamics of pipe flow driven by cardiac-cycle-inspired waveforms. Four cases with and without a low-flow plateau span two Reynolds-number ranges. The response follows four stages of turbulent--turbulent reorganisation. Strong acceleration suppresses transverse fluctuations and vortical activity. During acceleration and early deceleration, streamwise-normal-stress production recovers ahead of pressure--strain redistribution and radial momentum transport, allowing energy to accumulate in elongated streaks. In early deceleration, near-wall high-speed streaks develop predominantly varicose disturbances associated with Q4 sweeps, whereas outer-buffer-layer low-speed streaks develop predominantly sinuous disturbances associated with Q2 ejections. The transition exhibits distinct radial sequences: Q2-based local onset occurs progressively later towards the wall, whereas Q4-based onset is nearly simultaneous across the viscous sublayer and buffer layer, with peaks occurring successively outwards. The two responses overlap between the drag minimum and recovery maximum as redistribution intensifies markedly and multiscale momentum transport recovers rapidly. Turbulence then decays and its scales readjust. Where present, the plateau prolongs this decay and weakens the turbulence inherited by the next acceleration stage. It further delays local instability and lengthens the onset-to-peak intervals of the shear contributions. An unsteady friction decomposition links these phase-dependent dynamics to the drag response, highlighting the role of delayed turbulent shear recovery in sustaining the low-drag interval.

items.title: SATE: Transferable Spin-Adapted Neural Wavefunctions
items.summary: Accurate prediction of molecular reactivity requires both accurate and computationally efficient description of electron correlation and spin across various molecular geometries and electronic states. We introduce SATE, a spin-adapted transferable neural wavefunction architecture with effective core potentials. SATE combines a transferable neural wavefunction, the spin-adapted antisymmetrization method, and effective core potentials into a single foundation model architecture pretrained on compositions containing selected elements from hydrogen to bromine. After pretraining and adaptation, our model is able to predict 3d transition-metal spin-state gaps, bond dissociation energies, and reaction energies by addressing two key issues. First, including the core potentials into the model allows us to reduce the number of explicitly treated electrons. Second, using spin-adapted antisymmetrization enforces the prescribed total spin by construction. By testing our model with 3d transition metal chemistry, we evaluate our model's description of strong electron correlation and competing electronic states in such compounds. We find that pretraining improves most tested component energies at matched adaptation budgets, while improvements in spin-state gaps, dissociation energies, and reaction energies remain system dependent. Ultimately, our work lays the foundation for more accurate and transferable modeling of molecular systems by combining the computational efficiency of effective core potentials with explicit control over total spin.

items.title: A Mathematical Multiscale Framework for Nonlinear Modeling of the Heliosphere
items.summary: The inner heliosphere is a highly nonlinear continuous medium where macroscopic ideal magnetohydrodynamics is inextricably coupled with microscopic, fully developed stochastic turbulence. State-of-the-art global 3D numerical solvers, while proficient at capturing the large-scale propagation of extreme space physics phenomena such as coronal mass ejections and corotating interaction regions, are computationally constrained by grid resolution and fundamental partial differential equation formulations. Consequently, they inherently do not resolve the local small-scale turbulent cascade, magnetic intermittency, and localized thermodynamic anomalies. To bridge this fundamental scaleseparation gap, this paper presents a novel mathematical and numerical framework that harmoniously integrates global heliospheric structures with local turbulent physics. The framework generates a highly realistic synthetic continuous medium by superimposing a stochastically driven nonlinear turbulent cascade onto a bimodal deterministic background flow. This cascade reproduces theoretical constraints for fractional power spectral densities, magnetic compressibility, and small-scale intermittency via a discrete multiplicative binomial cascade (p-model). This multiscale continuous background is dynamically perturbed by analytical models of large-scale nonlinear transients, including kinematic shock steepening, continuous current sheet topological reversals, and solar ejecta formalized as asymmetric force-free magnetic flux ropes. By generating exact spatio-temporal arrays across arbitrary distributed coordinates, this unified mathematical model overcomes the spatial degeneracy of single-point observations and provides a computationally efficient analytical baseline for performance models supporting future in-situ multi-spacecraft heliospheric missions, which are currently in their feasibility study phase.

items.title: Rapid high-purity loading of barium ion via relayed selectivity from naturally abundant source
items.summary: Trapped ions is one of the promising platforms for realizing quantum information processing and quantum simulation. Selective and rapid loading of a specific isotope lays the critical foundation for such purpose particularly when scaling up the system size. Here we demonstrate a new method for rapid isotope-selective loading of $^{137}\mathrm{Ba}^{+}$ or $^{135}\mathrm{Ba}^{+}$, two types of promising ion qubits, from naturally abundant source using a three-step, ultraviolet-free photoionization scheme. Neutral atoms are selected on the narrow 791 nm $6s^2\,{}^1S_0\rightarrow6s6p\,{}^3P_1^o$ transition, resonantly transferred at 554 nm to $6s6d\,{}^3D_1$, and ionized using an existing 532 nm Raman beam. A spectral-overlap analysis based on isotope and hyperfine shifts shows relayed selectivity that the second step can further suppress undesired-isotope excitation and no contaminant ion is detected during our entire experiment. Besides, the resonant drive of the second step excitation yields a prominent loading rate of the selected species. This strategy using multi-step excitations to establish relayed selectivity can be extended to high-purity loading of other species of ions.

items.title: Characterizing sleep stages through the complexity--weighted-entropy plane in human intracranial data and in a whole-brain model
items.summary: Approaches based on symbolic information, such as entropy and complexity, have shown that sleep reorganizes the temporal structure of brain activity. However, most of this evidence comes from scalp EEG and group averages. In this work, we characterized sleep stages in intracranial recordings from 65 patients during wakefulness and the REM, N2, and N3 stages, using weighted permutation entropy (WPE) and the statistical complexity measure (SCM). In the complexity--entropy plane, the states formed a clear trajectory from wakefulness to REM, N2, and N3, with decreasing entropy and increasing complexity as sleep deepened. This organization was observed individually in most patients and was recovered more consistently by WPE than by conventional permutation entropy. The trajectory, however, was not the same throughout the cortex. All regions shifted in the same direction, but the occipital cortex followed a much shorter path than the parietal cortex. This result reflects the spatial heterogeneity of the brain during sleep and shows that cortical regions differ not only in the position they occupy in the plane, but also in the path they follow between states. Finally, a whole-brain model based on the human connectome showed that increasing neuronal adaptation shifts the simulated dynamics in the same direction observed in the empirical data, pointing to adaptation as one of the candidate mechanisms involved in this reorganization.

items.title: PI -- Multimodal Planetary Defense
items.summary: We present a practical and very effective method of planetary defense that allows for extremely short mitigation time scales, if required, as well as long time scale mitigation. One system allows for virtually any required defense mode. In general, it uses much less launch mass with vastly shorter required response time than classical deflection techniques The method uses an array of small hypervelocity kinetic penetrators that pulverize and disassemble an asteroid or small comet. This approach works in both long warning time, as well as in short warning scenarios with intercepts of minutes to days before impact. In longer time intercept scenarios, the disassembled asteroid fragments largely miss the Earth. In short intercept scenarios, the asteroid fragments of maximum $\sim$10-meter diameter allow the Earth's atmosphere to act as a "beam dump" with fragment burn up/ air burst, with energy primarily going into spatially and temporally de-correlated shock waves. The effectiveness of the approach depends on the intercept time and size of the asteroid but allows for effective defense against asteroids in the 20-1000m diameter class and could virtually eliminate the threat. While not recommended, a 20m diameter asteroid ($\sim$0.5Mt, similar to Chelyabinsk) can be mitigated with a 100s prior to impact intercept with a 10m/s disruption. With ~1m/s internal disruption, a 5 hour prior to impact intercept of a 50m diameter asteroid ($\sim$10Mt yield, similar to Tunguska), a 1 day prior to impact intercept of 100m diameter asteroid ($\sim$100Mt yield), a 20 day prior to impact intercept of Apophis ($\sim$370m diameter, $\sim$4Gt yield). The use of active (explosive) penetrators, including nuclear, allows the same system to mitigate extremely large threats. A "single launcher" solution to planetary defense using existing launch vehicles that achieve positive C3 becomes a viable option.

items.title: Elastic frontogenesis sets the spectra of smooth elastic turbulence
items.summary: Most turbulent flows are sustained by inertia, which transfers energy across scales and produces characteristic power-law spectra. Yet dilute polymer solutions also exhibit turbulence when inertia is negligible: in this state, known as elastic turbulence, the velocity field remains spatially smooth while both the velocity and the polymer conformation exhibit robust power-law spectra. How a smooth flow, lacking a hierarchy of eddies, generates such multiscale structure has remained unexplained. Here we show that the missing mechanism is elastic frontogenesis, whereby the flow spontaneously organizes polymer stress into thin sheets that are stretched within their plane and compressed across their thickness, causing their amplitude to grow as they become thinner. Because the fronts are sheet-like structures, this amplification-thinning law uniquely determines the polymer conformation spectrum, while the Stokes response transfers the same geometric scaling to the velocity field, reconciling broadband spectra with spatial smoothness. Being geometric rather than model-specific, elastic frontogenesis provides an organizing principle for viscoelastic flows and the viscoelastic analogue of vortex stretching in inertial turbulence.

items.title: Robust Implicit Neural Representation for Multiparameter Elastic Full-Waveform Inversion
items.summary: Multiparameter elastic full-waveform inversion (EFWI) provides a powerful means of reconstructing subsurface elastic properties, but its practical application remains challenging because of strong nonlinearity, parameter crosstalk, and the different sensitivities of seismic data to individual elastic parameters. We develop a robust implicit neural representation (INR) framework for multiparameter EFWI, using continuous neural representations to parameterize the subsurface model and provide an effective model-space constraint during inversion. Within this framework, we systematically investigate different elastic parameterizations and demonstrate that parameterization plays a critical role in controlling parameter coupling and inversion stability. Among the tested formulations, combining P-wave velocity (Vp), P-wave impedance (Ip), and the Vs/Vp ratio provides the most robust overall performance, yielding improved parameter separation and more reliable reconstruction of elastic properties. We evaluate the proposed approach on the Marmousi and Overthrust models under increasingly challenging inversion conditions and further apply it to the field Volve ocean-bottom-node dataset. Both synthetic and field-data results demonstrate that the INR-based formulation, together with the Vp-Ip-Vs/Vp parameterization, improves inversion stability, suppresses parameter cross-talk and inversion artifacts, and produces geologically coherent multiparameter models. These results highlight the importance of jointly considering model representation and physical parameterization in multiparameter EFWI and demonstrate the potential of robust INR-based inversion for complex synthetic and field seismic applications.

items.title: Crowding limits relative bacterial surface accumulation with density-induced effective heating
items.summary: The accumulation of microswimmers near walls has been studied for decades. While hydrodynamics and single-cell kinematics are well-explored, the role of cell-cell interactions remains understudied. However, in realistic, crowded environments such as the human gut, these interactions can be just as crucial. Here, we demonstrate that they actively weaken bacterial surface accumulation. Analysis of entrapped cell tracks reveals that crowding enhances orientational fluctuations, which increase the effective rotational diffusion and facilitate wall escape. A minimal model shows that this collective effect is equivalent to raising the system's effective temperature with density.

items.title: Ensemble Covariance Propagation with Machine Learning Weather Prediction Models in a Realistic Data Assimilation System
items.summary: Integrating machine learning weather prediction (MLWP) models into classical data assimilation (DA) workflows requires that they accurately evolve ensemble covariances. We evaluate this capability in a two-way coupled DA system, where an ensemble variational (EnVar) component evolves the mean and an ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF) evolves the covariances. The system is cycled over one month and assimilates a wide range of real-world observations, including microwave radiances. Using the MLWP model GraphCast for the EnKF and the physics-based MPAS model for the EnVar yields ensemble spread and covariances comparable to a reference configuration in which MPAS evolves both components. The resulting EnVar mean achieves consistently lower RMSE against GFS analyses, except near the model top, where spurious correlations degrade performance. These results demonstrate that MLWP models can propagate covariance information in a realistic DA cycling system and provide a proof of concept for their integration into future operational ensemble systems.

items.title: The Minimal Persona: Rarer and Shared Labels Both Skew Allocation Among AI Agents
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents built on large language models increasingly work in teams, where one agent divides tasks or resources among others that the software marks with a team, a role or a similar label. A model that simply up-weights any recipient sharing a string with its own context would favor same-label peers, so a shared-label tilt alone says little about groups. Borrowing the minimal-group paradigm of social psychology, we had six language models divide 100 points among 19 peers that differed only in carrying one of two invented words, in groups of unequal size (32,400 decisions). Varying group size separates two effects. In five of the six models, at the most unequal split, a recipient with the rarer label received 1.3 to 3.3 times the points of one with the common label even when the decider was not told its own label: a rarity effect that involves no match to the decider. In four of them it accounts for 35% to 55% of the extra favoritism that agents in the smaller group show their own group, and for more in the fifth. Telling the decider its label adds an own-group effect, positive in every model and in five of the six indistinguishable from label matching. With the labels hidden, neither appears. Because the labels mean nothing, bias tests built on lists of named social groups are not designed to detect either effect.

items.title: Work needed to lift a mass in Schwarzschild spacetime
items.summary: We determine the work needed to lift a mass from $r_2$ to $r_1$ in Schwarzschild spacetime in three ways. First we use a winch and a light rope. Then we use a photon collision. Finally we let the mass decay into photons and reconstruct it at the higher radius. All three methods give the same local work at $r_1$, $W_1=mc^2[1-N(r_2)/N(r_1)]$, where $N(r)=\sqrt{1-r_s/r}$. Thus, independently of $r_1$, the work tends to $mc^2$ as $r_2$ approaches the horizon. The rope example also gives a useful general-relativistic version of a simple machine: a rope in equilibrium need not have equal local forces at its two ends. The redshift factor plays the role of the lever arm. For a real rope the energy conditions prevent the tension from decreasing with height, so this lever advantage is confined to the idealization. The examples are intended as teaching material for undergraduate relativity courses.

items.title: Velocity gradient tensor reconstruction from tracer orientations via Jeffery dynamics
items.summary: The velocity gradient tensor is a local quantity, but methods that obtain it by spatial differencing of the velocities of spherical tracers amplify measurement noise. We propose a method that reconstructs the velocity gradient tensor from the orientations of non-spherical tracers such as flakes and rods. Based on the Jeffery-type equation, we show that, for incompressible flow, all components of the velocity gradient tensor are uniquely determined from the orientations of four tracers and their time derivatives in the neighbourhood of a reference point (orientation-based method). The method uses neither tracer positions nor spatial differencing. It therefore requires orientation measurements only near the reference point, without requiring measurements throughout a three-dimensional region, and measurement noise is amplified only through temporal differencing. Consequently, the minimum achievable error scales as $σ^{1/2}$ with the noise level $σ$, compared with $σ^{1/3}$ for the positional PTV-plus-differencing approach (position-based method). Numerical tests further show that the vorticity is reconstructed more accurately than by the position-based method, whereas the strain rate is reconstructed with comparable accuracy. Finally, applying the method to spherical Couette flow, we find that the reconstruction fails where the neighbouring tracers align, which renders the inversion ill-conditioned, and that this degeneracy appears as the characteristic light-and-dark pattern familiar from flow visualization.

items.title: Competing Influence in LLM Populations: Budget Timing and Baseline Drift
items.summary: When competing campaigns target a population of large language model (LLM) agents, observed opinion changes may reflect both campaign influence and changes that would occur without intervention. We study how the timing of campaign expenditure and the population's own evolution shape outcomes in a network of persona-conditioned LLM agents that exchange and revise opinions in natural language. A proponent and a challenger are tasked with generating opposing messages under equal delivery budgets, while a separate stance probe measures opinions without influencing the simulation. Across eight claims, we compare single-campaign and competitive conditions against matched no-campaign runs, and evaluate all nine combinations of early, sustained, and late spending on a reference topic. Baseline stance drift varies substantially across claims and, on some, accounts for a sizeable fraction of apparent campaign effects. After accounting for this drift, the direction of observed campaign-associated changes aligns more closely with the claim's epistemic standing than with the campaigner's assigned role. Uninfluenced populations also consistently lose stance diversity, demonstrating that directional opinion change and convergence are distinct phenomena. In networks with two opinion-segregated communities, campaigns primarily reduce differences between communities rather than diversity within them. LLM campaign agents do not always argue for their assigned positions, particularly when these conflict with established evidence. Finally, campaign outcomes depend on the opponent's expenditure schedule: unlike a matched numerical bounded-confidence population receiving interventions at the same times and locations, the LLM population exhibits a payoff structure with no pure-strategy equilibrium.

items.title: GPU acceleration of the numerical-atomic-orbital DFT code OpenMX with GEMMul8: performance and numerical agreement on consumer and HPC GPUs
items.summary: We integrate GEMMul8, a library that emulates FP64 matrix multiplication on INT8 Tensor Cores, into the GPU version of the numerical-atomic-orbital first-principles code OpenMX 4.0. The GEMMul8 configuration is compared against the cuBLAS FP64 configuration within each of two environments, a consumer GeForce RTX 5080 and an HPC-oriented H100 PCIe, for the four computational paths formed by collinear (CL) or noncollinear (NCL) spin and band or $Γ$-point-cluster solvers. In fixed-work measurements that completed 25 SCF iterations, the diagonalization section of a 384-atom CL band calculation on the RTX 5080 is accelerated by a factor of 2.1 and the total run time by 1.8; a 512-atom CL cluster calculation, which uses only real matrix products in contrast to the CL band calculation, still gains a factor of 1.5 in the diagonalization section. On the H100, GEMMul8 provides little additional acceleration of the diagonalization section. In an accuracy test on a 216-atom Si system in which one atom was displaced by 0.05 angstrom, all 24 configurations were converged using an SCF convergence criterion of $10^{-8}$; every configuration converged at the same iteration within each path, and the differences between GEMMul8 and cuBLAS are at most $2\times10^{-12}$ Ha in the total energy and $7\times10^{-12}$ Ha/Bohr in force components.

items.title: Time-resolved infrared spectroscopy with entangled photons and visible-light detection
items.summary: Time-resolved infrared (TR-IR) spectroscopy reveals molecular structural changes and charge-carrier dynamics on their intrinsic timescales, in photosynthesis, catalysis and optoelectronic materials, but requires complex sources of ultrashort infrared pulses, cryogenically cooled detectors to overcome thermal background, and intense probes that can perturb the sample. Quantum infrared spectroscopy avoids these constraints: harnessing quantum interference between the generation processes of frequency-entangled photon pairs, it reads out the infrared response of a sample by detecting only the visible partner photon, for which efficient detectors exist. To date, it has been limited to steady-state measurements. Here we demonstrate its ultrafast, time-resolved form with a picosecond visible pump pulse and a silicon detector. Each visible pulse generates photon pairs within a picosecond window; the infrared photon of a pair probes the excited sample at a set delay after excitation, and the transient response is read out from the count rate of its visible partner. We resolve picosecond carrier dynamics in a semiconductor saturable absorber mirror near 1529 nm with a picowatt-level probe, unaffected by thermal background and by sample IR photoluminescence 50 times stronger than the probe. The approach is applicable to the mid-infrared, fingerprint region, where infrared detection is hardest, and to the terahertz region.

items.title: Lensless single-pixel imaging through dynamic coded-aperture illumination
items.summary: We demonstrate a lensless single-pixel imaging (SPI) system combining dynamic coded-aperture illumination with single-pixel detection. Binary digital micromirror device (DMD) masks generate tailored grayscale intensity fields through coherent propagation, without relay projection optics or temporal grayscale synthesis. Six target-field configurations---uniform, Rayleigh speckle, squared-Rayleigh speckle, and sparse binary fields with $p=10\%$, $5\%$, and $1\%$---are evaluated using binary and grayscale objects. Intensity-correlation and nonnegative total-variation-regularized reconstructions reveal that the preferred illumination depends on the object, reconstruction method, and evaluation metric. By combining rapid binary modulation, programmable grayscale illumination, and single-pixel readout, this implementation provides a flexible architecture for lensless computational imaging and joint design of optical encoding and reconstruction.

items.title: More particles or the pair? An exact test of how to improve mode-coupling theory
items.summary: How a dense liquid arrests into a glass remains a central problem in physics. Mode-coupling theory (MCT), the leading microscopic theory of the glass transition, fails to reproduce mean-field caging. Two routes are proposed to repair it: tracking more-particle correlations, or enforcing repulsion within each colliding pair. Testing both on an exact benchmark liquid, we show that MCT lets touching spheres pass through each other at all orders: adding particles dilutes memory and worsens the transition, whereas restoring pair impenetrability recovers mean-field arrest and the cage size.

items.title: Origin of devil's staircases and anomalous Arnold tongues of breathing solitons in optical Kerr resonators
items.summary: Synchronization phenomena are ubiquitous across natural and engineered systems, and optical resonators supporting breathing solitons offer a natural platform for their investigation. In driven Kerr cavities described by the Lugiato-Lefever equation (LLE), breathing-soliton dynamics constitute a minimal setting in which such behavior can be systematically analyzed. Despite recent observations of intricate self-synchronization structures in mode-locked lasers-such as subharmonic entrainment, devil's staircases, and holes within Arnold tongues, i.e., regions of unsynchronized dynamics embedded within synchronized domains-their physical origin has remained elusive due to the complexity of laser dynamics. Here, we demonstrate that these phenomena emerge in the universal framework of the LLE. By reducing the problem to this model, we uncover the mechanism responsible for both the devil's staircase and the formation of holes within Arnold tongues. This provides a unified physical picture of synchronization in nonlinear systems, extending beyond optics and providing insight into analogous predictions and observations in fluids and other oscillatory media. In addition, we identify the regimes of high-order synchronization, enabling the generation of ultradense frequency combs, opening new directions for precision photonic applications.

items.title: Wide Field 3D Color Topography for Large-Angle Structures
items.summary: Three-dimensional (3D) topography measurement is essential for industrial inspection and scientific research. However, existing techniques are limited by an inherent trade-off between resolution, speed, color imaging capability and the ability to measure large-angle surfaces. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel method that integrates ring light illumination based wide-field 3D imaging with an iterative shape-from-focus (SFF) algorithm. The system employs coaxial epi-illumination combined with ring light illumination to simultaneously acquire information from flat regions and steep slopes. The proposed iterative SFF algorithm achieves high-resolution 3D topography measurement. Full-color 3D reconstructions of electronic chips and PCBs demonstrate that the proposed method enables fast scanning and sub-micrometer resolution and significantly extending the measurable inclination range for large-angle structures. This method fills a critical gap in existing technology for fast, natural-color, 3D imaging and measurement of samples with steep topographies.

items.title: Three-dimensional polarization of thermal fields at arbitrary distances from thin-film emitters
items.summary: Recent advances have shown that thermal radiation can exhibit strong polarization in both the near and far fields. However, most existing studies focus on paraxial far-field emission, where polarization can be described using conventional two-dimensional (2D) Stokes parameters. Non-paraxial thermal radiation, with three nonzero vector components, requires a fully three-dimensional (3D) polarization description. This work develops a generalized theoretical method for analyzing thermal-radiation polarization at arbitrary distances from an emitter. Fluctuation-dissipation theory is employed to determine the $3\times3$ coherence matrix of the thermally emitted electromagnetic field, from which generalized 3D Stokes parameters are obtained. This method is applied to planar slabs composed of isotropic, anisotropic, and nonreciprocal materials. The results reveal distinct polarization behavior across the near- and far-field regimes. Near-field polarization is strongly influenced by evanescent waves and polariton dispersion, whereas far-field polarization is primarily governed by polarization-dependent radiative properties, including differences between transverse-electric (TE) and transverse-magnetic (TM) emission. Slab thickness further modifies polarization by controlling supported modes and interference effects. In addition, circular polarization, which vanishes in reciprocal slabs, is observed in n-type doped InAs under an external magnetic field that breaks reciprocity. This work provides a unified framework for characterizing the polarization of thermal electromagnetic fields from the extreme near field to the far field.

items.title: Energy-conserving scheme for a shallow-water model with capillary effects
items.summary: We consider numerical approximations of shallow-water and thin-film flow models with capillary effects. These models lead to third-order differential equations, and we work with an augmented model with second-order derivatives. For a wide class of such models, which includes the classical shallow-water model and thin-film flow models under gravitational force, we develop a fully discrete energy-conserving scheme for both the quadratic and fully nonlinear capillary models. Numerical results show that the proposed scheme is stable and conserves total energy in the absence of dissipative effects.

items.title: Broad-angle photon-pair generation from high-$Q$ flatband resonant 3R-MoS$_{2}$ metasurfaces
items.summary: Spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) in ultrathin optical resonant metasurfaces offers a promising platform for integrated quantum light sources. However, conventional resonances suffer from steep momentum dispersion, limiting photon-pair generation to narrow excitation and emission angles. Here, we demonstrate a high-$Q$ flatband resonant 3R-MoS$_{2}$ metasurface for high-efficiency, broad-angle SPDC photon-pair generation. By combining Brillouin zone folding with in-plane symmetry breaking, we engineer a high-$Q$ flatband resonance in the near-infrared regime, maintaining a robust $Q$-factor across a wide range of incident angles. Exploiting the strong local electric field enhancement of resonance and the large second-order susceptibility of 3R-MoS$_{2}$, the metasurface boosts the degenerate SPDC pair-generation rate with orders of magnitude enhancement over an unpatterned film of identical thickness. Crucially, the near-zero band dispersion extends the effective emission angle to $\pm 5^{\circ}$ with negligible spectral drift $\sim 0.1$ nm and high directional tolerance. Under pulsed excitation with a finite spectral bandwidth, the metasurface maintains a substantial bandwidth-averaged photon-pair yield, while demonstrating strong spectral locking of the resonant emission channel against pump wavelength detuning despite the expected trade-off in generation efficiency. This work establishes a versatile strategy for momentum-independent quantum light sources, opening new avenues for scan-free quantum ghost imaging and quantum information processing.

items.title: Implementation Science Driven Identification of Barriers to AI Diagnostic Decision Support: A Stakeholder-Informed Concept Mapping Study
items.summary: The clinical translation of artificial intelligence (AI) is a critical step toward precision medicine. The implementation study presented here focuses specifically on barriers to AI adoption in the diagnostic medicine workflow. Successful clinical adoption of AI requires more than technical performance; it depends on addressing real-world organizational, ethical, infrastructural, and workflow-related barriers that may prevent promising systems from moving beyond research settings. To examine these barriers, we used structured concept mapping (CM) to operationalize stakeholder engagement and to integrate a knowledge translation (iKT) approach within the Knowledge-to-Action (KTA) framework. Stakeholders co-generated 96 statements describing barriers to AI implementation and organized them into 11 clusters, including infrastructure limitations, ethical and legal concerns, workflow integration challenges, and distrust in algorithmic reasoning. These findings provide actionable knowledge for supporting AI implementation in the diagnostic chain. We additionally position digital twins (DT) as a related, forward-looking context, as they are increasingly discussed as future extensions of AI-enabled care. As such, our findings offer preliminary insights for future DT deployment, as many DT systems are expected to rely on AI-driven prediction, multimodal data integration, and iterative model refinement. Addressing the identified barriers early may help AI-based clinical tools, and eventually DT-enabled applications, progress from prototypes toward evidence-based standards of care.

items.title: Wavelength-resolved polarization characterization of supercontinuum vector beams
items.summary: The polarization state of a supercontinuum (SC) vector beam provides a reference for quantitative polarimetry. We characterize an azimuthally polarized SC vector beam generated with an S-waveplate and azimuthal polarizers by wavelength-resolved Stokes imaging. Representative maps show an approximately tangential azimuthal angle and a small ellipticity parameter over much of the beam, together with the degree of polarization. The {\pm} 90° azimuthal angle boundary shifts by about 21° between 450 and 766 nm. A linear fit gives 21° {\pm} 7°, where the uncertainty is derived from the slope confidence interval and does not include uncharacterized systematic errors. Jones-matrix calculations examine candidate imperfections under specified assumptions. Attributing the measured boundary shift to this mechanism requires an intensity extinction ratio of about 7 or less at 766 nm if the offset at 450 nm is negligible and the shift corresponds to a uniform azimuthal angle change. The origin remains unresolved. The results motivate wavelength-dependent characterization and calibration of this probe for quantitative polarimetry.

items.title: Thermochemical Rossby waves in rapid rotation: from swallowtail geometry to nonlinear selection
items.summary: When heat and solute both destabilise a rapidly rotating fluid, do their buoyancies add? Codensity models assume so, giving a straight onset diagonal; spherical shells show curved and kinked thresholds. We study the Busse--Simitev rotating annulus, whose normal modes obey an exact complex cubic dispersion relation. Combining the Bilharz criterion with the neutral-curve envelope yields, in the rapid-rotation limit, an explicit swallowtail wave front, in Arnold's sense, that bends the codensity diagonal into smooth and then kinked thresholds as the diffusivity ratio decreases. Its cusp edges lie inside the unstable domain and its exposed kink ends at the swallowtail singularity; these are singularities of wave-number selection, without coalescence of temporal eigenvalues, and the swallowtail diffusivity ratio has analytical small- and large-Prandtl-number limits. At a kink, broad, fast thermal and narrow, slow compositional Rossby waves become neutral together; hidden arcs mark the birth and merger of unstable wave-number bands. The same geometry enters nonlinear selection: mean-scalar feedback factors through neutral-arc normals and scalar responses, so the mean-profile coexistence margin vanishes with the kink angle as the waves merge. Complete cubic coefficients predict robust coexistence at a reference corner and a narrow bistable interval near merger. Exact finite-rotation corners and periodic-cell simulations confirm the coexisting waves and their invasion thresholds.

items.title: A Differentiable DFT-Based Framework for Inverse Materials Design
items.summary: Discovering solid-state materials with target properties remains a central challenge in computational materials science. Existing data-driven approaches rely on training data and may generalize poorly outside the training distribution. Here we develop a first-principles inverse-design framework that requires no training data. It integrates reverse-mode automatic differentiation (AD) into the Korringa--Kohn--Rostoker method combined with the coherent potential approximation (KKR-CPA), in which elemental concentrations serve as continuous optimization variables. Reverse-mode AD computes all concentration gradients in one backward pass, enabling optimization over dozens of candidate elements. Any differentiable quantity computable within KKR-CPA can serve as an optimization objective. We demonstrate this generality in permanent-magnet and half-metal design, identifying candidates such as (Nd$_{0.983}$Pr$_{0.017}$)(Co$_{0.72}$Fe$_{0.28}$)$_2$Fe$_3$ and FeMn(As$_{0.83}$P$_{0.17}$), respectively. We also synthesized materials with five SmCo$_5$-based compositions selected during optimization for higher magnetization. Their measured magnetization agreed closely with calculated values. Our framework offers a first-principles route to designing materials with target properties.

items.title: Integer electron-count cuts in variational second-order reduced-density-matrix theory. II. A convergent hierarchy of rigorous relaxations for real-space pair-density representability
items.summary: Variational second-order reduced-density-matrix calculations can dissociate molecules into fractionally charged fragments; Part I largely removed this failure with integer electron-count conditions on fixed partitions. Building on the realizability theory of point processes, we place these conditions in a convergent hierarchy of rigorous relaxations, defined by finite occupation linear programs (LPs) on spatial partitions, for real-space pair densities at fixed one-particle density. Every level contains all representable pair densities, the levels tighten under nested refinement, and their intersection characterizes pair densities admitting a symmetric $N$-particle probability-measure extension. In a fixed orbital basis the levels give monotonically increasing lower bounds to the full configuration-interaction energy, which they need not reach, even for the Coulomb repulsion. The spin-summed real-space cuts of Part I are its two-cell members. The LP optimum is also a measure: at fixed one-particle density it equals the $L^1$ distance of the coarse-grained candidate from representability and increases under refinement to that of the candidate, with a vanishing coarse-graining error; its primal law constructs a representable approximation, and its dual a violated valid inequality, used as a cut in molecular calculations. The count conditions are not implied by the usual positivity conditions: moment data that satisfy all three-particle positivity conditions, including $T_1$ and $T_2$, give through Gaussian orbitals a smooth pair density that violates an integer count. For atoms at fractional electron number, ensemble relaxations with the integer-count condition lie closer to the exact piecewise-linear energy than the zero-variance fixed-$N$ form.

items.title: Breakeven complexity: A new perspective on neural partial differential equation solvers
items.summary: Neural surrogate solvers of partial differential equations (PDEs) promise dramatic speedups over numerical methods, especially in scenarios requiring many solves. However, current accuracy-based evaluations do not fully consider two central issues: (1) neural solvers incur substantial up-front costs for data generation, training, and tuning; and (2) classical solvers can also generate low-fidelity solutions at a sufficiently low simulation cost. To explicitly account for these realities and fully incorporate end-to-end costs, we propose an evaluation framework centered on breakeven complexity, a metric that counts the forward solves before a learned solver is cost-effective relative to an error-equivalent traditional solver. To evaluate this measure, we apply scaling laws to determine how much training budget to allocate to data generation and discuss how to achieve smooth error-matching in diverse settings. We evaluate the breakeven complexity of multiple neural PDE solvers on three PDEs on 2D periodic domains from APEBench and a novel benchmark of flows past multiple obstacles generated by the GPU-native PyFR code. Among other findings, our results suggest that neural PDE solvers become more effective as problems get harder in terms of cost, dimension, rollout, physics regime (e.g. higher Reynolds number), etc.

items.title: A Sequential Monte Carlo Method for Data Assimilation in Subsurface Flow Systems with Hierarchical Uncertainty
items.summary: Subsurface flow systems often involve hierarchical geological uncertainty, meaning both higher-level metaparameters and cell-by-cell properties are uncertain. This leads to challenges for data assimilation because both sets of parameters must be estimated. In this work we develop an adaptive-tempered sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) procedure for joint Bayesian estimation of these quantities. The method uses noncentered geological parameterizations, with geomodel realizations represented by metaparameters and Gaussian latent variables that are independent under the prior. Adaptive likelihood tempering, importance weighting, resampling, and blockwise Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) mutation are applied at each iteration. Flow surrogates are used for all function evaluations. The hierarchical SMC procedure is further extended to treat successive data assimilation. In this case, existing posterior particles are updated in a manner that accounts for correlations in surrogate model errors across observation batches. We consider two distinct 3D systems with hierarchical uncertainty. The first is a faulted carbon storage system containing three stacked aquifers and two extensive faults. Principal component analysis is used to represent target-aquifer heterogeneity, while geological metaparameters characterize uncertain aquifer and fault properties. The second is a channelized oil-water system containing three facies with uncertain properties. A latent diffusion model represents variability in channel geometry and facies realizations. For the four synthetic true models considered, SMC posterior metaparameter distributions and flow predictions agree closely with reference MCMC results. SMC, however, requires fewer function evaluations and provides speedups of 2.5--7.0 for single-stage data assimilation. Even greater speedups are achieved with multiple GPUs.

items.title: Toward Self-Evolving Geospatial Algorithms: An LLM-Driven Framework with a Case Study on Spatial Regime Discovery
items.summary: Geospatial algorithms have been developed through expert-driven discovery: a researcher spots a limitation, proposes a structural fix, and checks it by hand. With LLM-driven multi-agent systems becoming practical, much of the candidate-generation, evaluation, and selection work can now be largely automated, while the researcher's role shifts upstream toward problem formulation, evaluation design, and interpretation. We refer to this paradigm as Self-Evolving Geospatial Algorithms (SEGA) and propose a framework with three required modules: a two-loop architecture with embedded geographic knowledge as the inner-loop engine; an automatic code formatter that converts any raw geospatial algorithm into the standardized triple required by the inner loop; and a simulation-driven training protocol, in which evolution runs only on synthetic data with known ground truth, and the discovered algorithm is applied unchanged to real data, keeping real-world results out-of-sample. We use spatial regime discovery as a case study, seeded with the Two-stage K-Models algorithm. Evolution uses the Rand Index against the ground-truth partition as fitness signal; the frozen algorithm is then evaluated on 150 simulated grids and 11 real-world datasets across climate, health, hydrology, and politics. The evolved algorithm outperforms its seed, knowledge-free baselines, and four classical regionalization methods. Ablations further indicate that the channel of geographic-knowledge injection, structured retrieval versus prompt-level hints, is itself load-bearing. In this case study, LLM-assisted search sped up the inner loop; whether it does so for other seeds and task families remains open. The geographer's role -- asking the right questions, designing trustworthy evaluation -- grows more central.

items.title: The AI research space shapes country academic performance
items.summary: Recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI) have demonstrated great potential across diverse domains, prompting increasing attention to understanding the AI ecosystem. As knowledge production is often perceived as a process of connecting existing pieces of knowledge, mapping the interconnections of AI knowledge is crucial for unraveling the dynamics of scientific production in AI. However, maps created so far have fallen short of capturing knowledge relatedness, focusing instead on citation relationships between subfields. Here, we build an AI research space by connecting pairs of AI research topics based on their proximity measured through author-topic coupling. Projections of country level performances onto the space reveal that countries exhibit distinct baskets of specializations. We further examine the role of the structure of the AI research space in the scientific development of nations. We find that countries are more likely to gain specialization in topics that have high proximity to already specialized neighbor topics, and that publications whose topics align more with the developed topics in the country are more likely to become high impact. Our results highlight the AI development gaps across nations and the path-dependence in the development induced by the AI research space.

items.title: Hyperelasticity as an efficient regularizer for 2D-3D thoracic motion models
items.summary: Patient-specific motion models enable real-time volumetric imaging of the thorax from a single x-ray projection, but most existing approaches require hours of training. The VM-DS framework trains in minutes, yet its image-space self-consistency regularizer accounts for 40% of the motion-model fitting time and does not prevent the fitted fields from folding. In this paper, we explore a range of regularization approaches including scaling-and-squaring, bending energy, diffusion, first-order inverse consistency, isotropic total variation, a negative-Jacobian hinge, |log det J|, a control-point injectivity bound and hyperelastic regularization. Hyperparameters were selected on two development cases from the public DIR-Lab 4D dataset under rules fixed in advance, and the regularizers were tested on eight held-out cases. At a fixed number of training steps, the hyperelastic term trained in 5.6 against 8.4 min and gave a lower held-out TRE (2.5 mm). With a quarter of the motion-model budget it matched the baseline (2.7 mm), and at every budget from 2 to 17 min its mean TRE was lower by 0.3-0.5 mm. Hyperelastic fields had no folded voxel in any held-out view, whereas baseline fields folded in 83 % of views, with image similarity unchanged. A hyperelastic volume penalty can therefore replace image-space self-consistency, matching accuracy with 3-5 minutes of training and removing folding, bringing on-the-day motion models closer to routine use in image-guided interventions. Code will be available at https://github.com/Image-X-Institute/Voxelmap/tree/hyper

items.title: Bright and Dark Excitons in CrSBr: Local Ligand-Field Character and Band-Coherent Optical Selection Rules
items.summary: Magnetic van der Waals semiconductors such as CrSBr host an intricate exciton landscape. Quasiparticle self-consistent GW theory with electron-hole ladder vertex corrections (QSGWc) has established the gap and the character of the bright XA (1.34 eV) and XB (1.8 eV) excitons. Why these bright excitons coexist, within a few tens of meV, with companions orders of magnitude darker has remained unexplained.
