The rescaled radial distance from the disk boundary has an exponential limiting distribution, while the rescaled angular deviations from each main ray are Gaussian. Inspired by logarithmic tracts in the Eremenko-Lyubich class $\mathcal{B}$, we pull exterior sectors back conformally to countably many curvilinear strips extending in finitely many directions and obtain zero-counting asymptotics in each strip, although the coefficients may lie outside this class. Moreover, the asymptotic formula for the global zero count and the joint limit in radius and angle persist under arbitrary entire perturbations of strictly smaller weighted exponential type.

items.title: Stochastic Multilevel Sampling for Inverse Problems via Coarse-Space Identifiability
items.summary: Sampling only part of the data reduces the cost of each iteration in an inverse problem, but can make reconstruction updates unreliable. We study stochastic multilevel sampling, which computes updates on a coarse-to-fine hierarchy of correction spaces. The guiding idea is that a small sample may support a reliable coarse-grid update even when it provides insufficient information for a fine-grid update. For quadratic objectives, we identify conditions under which corrections computed from sampled data decrease the full-data objective. In small-batch experiments with computed tomography and periodic deblurring, the stochastic multilevel method improves reconstruction accuracy over matched single-level methods. In an increasingly ill-conditioned CT refinement with a fixed number of projection angles, the single-level error increases as the image dimension grows, whereas a deep hierarchy maintains or improves accuracy and outperforms full-data single-level optimization at the same number of forward and adjoint applications. The gains persist across the tested local solvers and strengthen with deeper hierarchies. A separate known-probe ptychography study provides complementary evidence for the benefit of hierarchical corrections for nonlinear inverse problems.

items.title: On the linearity of squarefree powers of edge ideals
items.summary: Let $G$ be a graph and $I(G)$ its edge ideal. The $p$-th squarefree power $I(G)^{[p]}$ is the monomial ideal generated by the squarefree monomials corresponding to the matchings of size $p$ of $G$. A central highlight of our work is the complete solution of a problem posed by Bigdeli, Herzog and Zaare-Nahandi in 2017, which asked to characterize when squarefree powers of edge ideals have the first syzygy module generated by linear forms. Moreover, for a $1$-dimensional flag simplicial complex $Δ$ and its Stanley--Reisner ideal $I_Δ$, which is the edge ideal of the complement graph of $Δ$, we prove that $I_Δ^{[p]}$ has a linear resolution if and only if it is linearly related and the $(2p-1)$-st homology of the neighbourhood complex of $Δ$ vanishes. As a consequence, we describe the shape of the Betti table of $I_Δ^{[p]}$, and we give a combinatorial characterization of when $I_Δ^{[p]}$ has a linear resolution, provided that the $2p$-core of $Δ$ has maximum degree at most $2p$. Finally, we show that no such characterization exists in general: the linearity of $I_Δ^{[2]}$ may depend on the characteristic of the field, and it cannot be described by finitely many forbidden induced subgraphs.

items.title: Multi-objective Markov Decision Process: Set-valued Bellman's principle and fixed point perspective
items.summary: We study infinite-horizon discounted Markov decision processes with multiple cost objectives and finite state and action spaces. We consider the set of value functions generated by randomized Markov policies, where each function describes the expected discounted costs from all initial states under a single policy. We establish a set-valued Bellman equation and characterize this set as the greatest fixed point of the associated Bellman operator. We also show that choosing an attainable cost vector separately for each initial state can produce a function that no single Markov policy realizes. Nevertheless, the attainable costs at individual states satisfy their own Bellman recursion. These results provide a dynamic programming and fixed point framework for multi-objective Markov decision processes.

items.title: Shape Holomorphy of the Calderón Projector on Lipschitz Surfaces: Frequency-Explicit Bounds for the Helmholtz
items.summary: We establish the holomorphic dependence of the Calderón projector for the Helmholtz operator upon shape boundary deformations of a family of bounded Lipschitz domains in two and three spatial dimensions, with bounds explicit in the wavenumber and the size of the holomorphic extension. More precisely, after transporting the four boundary integral operators contained in the Calderón projector to a fixed reference boundary, we prove that the resulting parameter-to-operator maps admit bounded holomorphic extensions in their natural fractional Sobolev spaces. Unlike approaches that require boundary regularity of class $\mathscr C^{1,1}$ or higher, our argument traces the holomorphic dependence on the shape by transferring elliptic estimates to the boundary through the fundamental solution and the Dirichlet and conormal trace operators. This construction is the key step that allows us to treat Lipschitz-regular boundary deformations. Furthermore, we show that the domain of holomorphy can be chosen independently of the wavenumber $κ$, while the operator bounds in the corresponding fractional Sobolev spaces contain algebraic factors in $κ$ multiplied by $\exp(Cκδ)$. In particular, for real domains, corresponding to $δ=0$, our single layer estimate recovers, to our knowledge, the best available frequency dependence on general Lipschitz boundaries. For the double layer, adjoint double layer, and hypersingular operators, we obtain novel frequency-explicit bounds. The results proved in this work provide the analytic foundation for frequency-explicit uncertainty quantification, model order reduction, and high-dimensional approximation of boundary integral operators, their Galerkin discretizations, and the resulting boundary densities and quantities of interest on families of parametrically varying boundaries.

items.title: The convergence-divergence criterion for the Mañé cohomology lemma and Livšic theorem
items.summary: We establish a dynamical convergence-divergence criterion for all functions with a prescribed modulus of continuity to have continuous sub-actions. The divergence part of the criterion, which gives functions that do not have any bounded sub-action, is valid for general dynamical systems with a weakly repelling fixed point. This unifies and generalises versions of the Mañé cohomology lemma for uniformly expanding maps, and results of Morris for maps with an indifferent fixed point. One consequence is that for any infinite compact metric space $(X,ρ)$, and Lipschitz Ruelle-expanding map $T:X\to X$, a metric transform $ω$ satisfies Dini's criterion $\int_0 ω(s)s^{-1}\, ds <\infty$ if and only if all functions that are Lipschitz for $ω\circρ$ have continuous sub-actions. Another consequence is that if $T$ is an expanding circle map of Manneville--Pomeau type $α\in(0,1)$, then $ω$ satisfies the convergence criterion $\int_0 ω(s)s^{-1-α}\, ds <\infty$ if and only if all functions that are Lipschitz for $ω\circρ$ have continuous sub-actions. For the latter class of maps, with $ω$ satisfying the convergence criterion, we prove a Livšic theorem for functions $f$ that are Lipschitz for $ω\circρ$: if $\int f\, dμ=0$ for all invariant measures $μ$, then $f=\varphi\circ T-\varphi$ for a function $\varphi$ that is Lipschitz with respect to $D_α(ω)\circρ$, where $D_α(ω)(t)= \int_0^t ω(s)s^{-1-α}\, ds$.

items.title: On Continuum Theories in a Locally Conformal Setting
items.summary: We study continuum and kinetic dynamics on locally conformally symplectic (LCS) and locally conformally cosymplectic (LCCos) manifolds. The main geometric tool is the Lichnerowicz-de Rham differential, which allows local geometric data that are compatible only up to conformal rescaling to glue into global structures. In the LCS setting, we analyze the locally conformal Vlasov equation from the viewpoint of continuity. Its source term does not represent particle creation or annihilation: it measures the mismatch between the ordinary phase-space volume and the conformally weighted volume determined by the Lee form. Absorbing this weight into the density yields a source-free continuity equation. We also compute the entropy production of the transported density, and illustrate the framework through a thermostatted ensemble, an LCS-driven Vlasov model with a momentum-dependent gyroscopic force, and their combination. We then propose a new definition of LCCos manifolds in which the defining one-form and two-form carry the same conformal weight. Unlike the usual convention, this allows local cosymplectic Hamiltonian systems to glue directly into global LCCos Hamiltonian dynamics, and it normalizes the evolution vector field by the conformal unit rather than by the ordinary unit. We develop the corresponding Hamiltonian, evolution and continuum dynamics, and illustrate them with a time-dependent mass example exhibiting transport in the distinguished time direction, momentum-space drift, and conformal source terms.

items.title: Common zeros of homogeneous polynomials and the weight hierarchy of projective Reed-Muller codes
items.summary: We determine the maximum number of common zeros in projective space of any set of linearly independent homogeneous polynomials of the same degree, when the degree is smaller than the cardinality of the finite field. This proves the conjecture of Beelen, Datta, and Ghorpade, resolving a longstanding problem on common zeros and determining the complete weight hierarchy of the corresponding projective Reed-Muller codes. The proof uses Green's hyperplane restriction bound, combined with a footprint argument that reduces the problem to the affine case solved by Heijnen and Pellikaan. Wei duality then determines the hierarchy in sufficiently large degrees, recovering the complete hierarchy in every degree for the projective plane. Finally, we prove an upper bound valid in every degree, and conjecture that it is always sharp.

items.title: Spanning triangulations in random graphs
items.summary: In 1991 Bollobás and Frieze found the threshold for the emergence of a spanning triangulation of a triangle in the binomial random graph, up to a logarithmic factor. In this paper, we find the threshold probability for the emergence of a spanning triangulation of a $k$-gon for any $3\leq k\leq n$, up to a constant factor.

items.title: Near-Purity Screening and Dominant-Atom Estimation in Softmax Mixtures and Their Ensembles
items.summary: We study near-purity screening and dominant-atom estimation in softmax mixtures, whose components share a common set of category features. A mixture is called $\varepsilon$-pure if one of its mixing weights is at least $1-\varepsilon$. We introduce the Trace of Latent Covariance Criterion ($\mathrm{TLC}^{2}$), a direct estimator of the trace of the covariance matrix of the latent mixing measure, constructed without estimating its atoms or weights, or knowing the number of components. Unlike existing moment-based approaches, our estimator is constructed for the softmax family and does not require knowledge or estimation of the feature distribution. We establish finite-sample guarantees for $\mathrm{TLC}^{2}$, showing that it achieves a parametric convergence rate up to an additive approximation error of order $p^{-1/2}$, without requiring minimum separation between mixture atoms. We also study estimation of the dominant atom in near-pure mixtures by fitting a single softmax component. We prove that the resulting maximum likelihood estimator has an error bound consisting of the usual parametric term and a bias term governed by the weighted distances between the dominant and remaining atoms, revealing adaptation to the geometry of the mixture. Finally, we extend near-purity screening and dominant-atom estimation to ensembles of softmax mixtures with shared atoms and mixture-specific weights. We apply $\mathrm{TLC}^{2}$ separately to each ensemble member to screen for near-purity without knowing the number of components. Under additional assumptions, clustering the resulting dominant-atom estimators yields finite-sample guarantees for estimating the shared atoms. An application to the Million Song Dataset illustrates how the estimated softmax directions reveal interpretable structure in the data.

items.title: The vector-valued Stein inequality and dimension-free R-sectoriality
items.summary: For a complex Banach space \(X\), we characterise dimension-free \(R\)-sectoriality of the Walsh operator, the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck operator, the Laplacian, and the Poisson operator by the vector-valued Stein inequality. For each family, the dimension-free \(R\)-bound of the resolvents on the negative real axis equals the Stein constant. Consequently, the resolvent estimate on the negative real axis already implies uniform \(R\)-sectoriality at an angle strictly smaller than \(π/2\). We furthermore prove that the full and dyadic Stein properties are equivalent and that they are independent of the exponent \(1<p<\infty\) entering their definition.

items.title: Continuum hierarchical Cannings process: I. Construction, duality and dichotomy
items.summary: We construct spatial measure-valued Cannings processes on the \emph{continuum} hierarchical group $Ω_N^\infty$ of order $N\in\N$ (an uncountable topological group with an ultrametric distance). These processes arise as the continuum-space limit of spatial Cannings processes on the \emph{discrete} hierarchical group $Ω_N$ of order $N\in\N$ (a countable topological group with an ultrametric distance) analysed in \cite{GHKK14}. On $Ω_N$, each site represents the \emph{geographic location} of a colony of individuals, each carrying a \emph{type} drawn from a compact type space $\K$, and the state in each colony is a probability measure on $\K$ describing the type distribution in that colony in the large-colony-size limit of individual-based models. The continuum-space processes on $Ω_N^\infty$ take values in the set of locally finite measures on $Ω_N^\infty \times \K$ and are to be thought of as describing a population of individuals, each equipped with a geographic location in $Ω_N^\infty$ and a type in $\K$, and each being subjected to \emph{migration} and three mechanisms of \emph{resampling}: (1) Fleming-Viot resampling at single sites; (2) Cannings resampling at single sites; (3) Cannings resampling and uniform reshuffling in balls around single sites (corresponding to consecutive hierarchical levels). The reshuffling adds to the migration, resulting in an \emph{effective migration} that is the superposition of the two relocation mechanisms.

items.title: The Geometric Deformation of Curved $L_\infty$ Algebras and Lie Algebroids
items.summary: While $L_\infty$ algebras are fundamental structures in differential geometry and mathematical physics, the geometric information encoded in such structures is often implicit. We address the following question: What constitutes a geometrically meaningful deformation of an $L_\infty$ algebra arising from vector bundles, and how can such deformations classify new geometric invariants? Inspired by nonabelian extension theory of Lie algebras, we define geometric deformations of curved $L_\infty$ algebras constructed from a vector bundle $V\to M$, and demonstrate that such deformations uniquely correspond to Lie algebroid structures on $V$. Explicit computations reveal that a representative of the first Atiyah-Chern class is exact in the total Weil complex, with its primitive representing the modular class in Lie algebroid cohomology. In the case of action Lie algebroids, the leading-order Atiyah-Chern classes correspond to the equivariant Chern characters. Applications to BV theories show that the geometric deformations naturally generate Poisson sigma models. These results provide a coherent framework for deriving field theories from geometric deformations of $L_\infty$ algebras.

items.title: Deterministic Principal Ideals of Dependent Random Operators
items.summary: We classify the algebraic principal ideals of alternating quadratic random operators under dimension-free two-sided curvature bounds. For the centered evaluation of a Hilbert two-form, an explicit covariance compensator determines the principal ideal after every fixed compact perturbation. For fixed spectral choices, the compensator is a compact linear function of the full covariance with explicit finite-dimensional approximation bounds; its class modulo the independent Gaussian ideal is intrinsic. For fixed spatial weights of rank at least two and a trace-class kernel, all attainable principal ideals form an exact order interval. Every intermediate ideal is realized by a Gaussian covariance arbitrarily close to the identity while each row retains its standard Gaussian law. For these spatial weights, trace class is also the exact kernel domain for raw evaluation under every law in the curvature class. The proof uses a conditional-residual criterion for linear operators, polarization, and finite-rank approximation. Applications include Wiener area and dependent matrices with doubly monotone variance weights. A logarithmic example separates principal ideals with identical membership in every Schatten class.

items.title: A Note on Singular Boundary Regularisation in Hamiltonian Systems
items.summary: Singular changes of variables in Hamiltonian systems, such as McGehee coordinates in celestial mechanics or renormalised variables in dispersive PDE blow-up, are designed to extend the equations of motion to a singular boundary. In contrast, it may be that near the boundary, the the induced symplectic two-form may rescale distinct geometric directions by distinct powers of the singular scale, and if the leading weighted part is degenerate, no single conformal factor makes the form extend as a smooth non-degenerate two-form. This anisotropic obstruction is complementary to the isotropic singularities studied in bm-symplectic geometry. We record it in an elementary finite-dimensional criterion and illustrate it with McGehee regularisation of homogeneous central-force collisions and, formally, with the modulation geometry of focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation blow-up.

items.title: Double-Scaling Limits for Monitored Haar Products
items.summary: We study products of independent Haar matrices interspersed with a fixed corank-one projection. As the matrix dimension $N$ and product length $L$ grow with $L/N\toτ$, we prove that the empirical distribution of squared singular values converges to the free multiplicative Poisson law with $S$-transform $S(z)=\exp(τ/(1+z))$, for both the unitary and orthogonal ensembles. Lagrange inversion yields its moments explicitly, proving Beenakker's conjectured Erlang formula for every moment order.

items.title: Smallest gaps of the two-dimensional Coulomb gas
items.summary: We consider the two-dimensional Coulomb gas with a general potential at the determinantal temperature, or equivalently, the eigenvalues of random normal matrices. We prove that the smallest gaps between particles are typically of order $n^{-3/4}$, and that the associated joint point process of gap locations and gap sizes, after rescaling the gaps by $n^{3/4}$, converges to a Poisson point process. As a consequence, we show that the $k$-th smallest rescaled gap has a limiting density proportional to $x^{4k-1}e^{-\frac{\mathcal{J}}{4}x^{4}}$, where $\mathcal{J}=π^{2}\int ρ(z)^{3}d^{2}z$ and $ρ$ is the density of the equilibrium measure. This generalizes a result of Shi and Jiang beyond the quadratic potential.

items.title: Perdomo's index conjecture for minimal hypersurfaces in spheres
items.summary: Let $x:M^n\to\sphere^{n+1}(1)$, $n\ge2$, be a full minimal immersion of a closed, connected, oriented manifold. We prove that its Morse index is at least $n+3$, with equality precisely for the standard Clifford embeddings. For a non-Clifford image, the constant function and the position and normal coordinates span a space containing an $(n+4)$-dimensional subspace on which the Jacobi quadratic form is negative definite.

items.title: Twisted convolution with conic support and the parabolic algebra
items.summary: We prove that tempered distributions on \(\mathbb R^{2n}\) whose supports satisfy a common strict cone condition form a unital associative algebra without zero divisors under twisted convolution \(\star\). The supports may be noncompact, and the associated Weyl maps need not be bounded. As applications, we show that the parabolic algebra and the norm-closed algebra generated by positive translations and modulations have no zero divisors, confirming Levene's conjecture. We also obtain a zero-product theorem for Toeplitz operators on the one-dimensional Fock space with bounded symbols whose distributional Fourier transforms satisfy a common strict cone condition. The proof of the distribution theorem uses Schwartz smoothing between distributional Weyl maps to convert a hypothetical zero product of nonzero distributions into a smooth function \(h\not\equiv0\) satisfying the same cone condition and \(h\star h=0\). The cone bound implies the \(Q\)-support condition, meaning that some linear functional is bounded above on \(\operatorname{supp}h\) and has compact upper level sets there. Truncating \(h\) near the maximum of this functional and applying the support identity for compactly supported twisted squares rule out \(h\star h=0\). For the operator applications, uniformly bounded Weyl-conjugation averages identify twisted convolution with bounded operator composition under the common cone condition.

items.title: Comparing algebraic cubature rules on spline curved elements
items.summary: We compare four methods for the construction of algebraic cubature rules on planar elements, whose boundary is tracked by splines. The methods, that we have developed over the last two decades, are based on Green theorem together with some cornerstones of polynomial approximation theory: Gaussian quadrature,Tchakaloff theorem, discretized Chebyshev expansion (hyperinterpolation), Fekete-like interpolation. We discuss their advantages and drawbacks in view of the application to curved polytopal element methods. We have also made freely available at a single site the corresponding open-source Matlab codes.

items.title: Abs-Smooth Frank-Wolfe Method: Primal-Dual Analysis, Heavy Ball Momentum, and Inexact Oracles
items.summary: We study projection-free optimization for convex objectives that satisfy abs-smoothness, a structural property that captures many non-smooth yet piecewise smooth functions arising, e.g., in modern machine learning models. We develop a unified framework for Abs-Smooth Frank-Wolfe methods, establishing a clean primal-dual analysis that guarantees convergence without requiring classical smoothness assumptions. Our framework extends the available results in two important directions. First, we introduce a heavy ball momentum variant and show that momentum can be incorporated naturally under abs-smoothness while preserving convergence guarantees. Second, we analyze inexact minimization oracles, demonstrating robustness to approximate inner solutions. Moreover, we relax the full convexity assumption and study the case where convexity holds only for the piecewise linear approximations of the objective, further broadening the applicability of conditional gradient methods to a wider class of non-smooth problems.

items.title: Heat equation from a deterministic dynamics
items.summary: We derive the heat equation for the thermal energy under diffusive space-time scaling for a purely deterministic microscopic dynamics satisfying Newton equations perturbed by an external chaotic force acting like a magnetic field.

items.title: Budan--Fourier theorem for circuit polynomial systems
items.summary: We prove a Budan--Fourier theorem for linear combinations of analytic functions whose successive Wronskians are positive: the number of zeros of $g=\sum_{k=1}^s c_kh_k$ in an interval $(a,b]$, counted with multiplicities, is bounded by the drop of the number of sign changes of the sequence of Wronskians $W(h_1,\ldots,h_{k-1},g)$ between $a$ and $b$, and the difference is even. This refines the bound $s-1$ of Koiran, Portier and Tavenas, and we show that it applies, after a suitable renumbering, to any sequence of functions satisfying Descartes' rule of signs. We then study the functions arising from polynomial systems supported on circuits, that is, systems of $n$ equations in $n$ variables with $n+2$ monomials. For these functions, we show that the Budan--Fourier bound never exceeds Descartes' bound, and we compute it at the endpoints of the interval of definition. As an application, we obtain a refinement of the optimal Descartes' rule of signs for circuits of Bihan, Dickenstein and Forsgård: we bound the number of positive solutions whose logarithm lies in explicit polytopes, these bounds add up to at most the bound of Bihan, Dickenstein and Forsgård, and they determine the parity of the number of positive solutions.

items.title: FEALPy.OPT: A Multi-Backend Tensor Computing Framework for Metaheuristic Optimization on CPU and GPU Platforms
items.summary: Metaheuristic algorithms (MAs) are widely used to solve complex optimization problems, but their computational costs can become substantial as population size and problem dimensionality increase. This paper presents FEALPy.OPT, an open-source Python framework for metaheuristic optimization built on the FEALPy computational infrastructure. It integrates a unified optimizer abstraction with multi-backend tensor computation, supporting NumPy and PyTorch backends on CPU and GPU platforms. To evaluate its computational performance, five metaheuristic algorithms are tested on ten benchmark functions under three problem scales, with population sizes ranging from 100 to 10,000 and dimensions from 30 to 100. The results show that NumPy/CPU achieves the shortest average runtime for small-scale problems, whereas PyTorch/GPU becomes increasingly advantageous as the problem scale grows. For large-scale problems, PyTorch/GPU is approximately 9.50 times faster than PyTorch/CPU and 32.96 times faster than NumPy/CPU. These findings demonstrate the value of multi-backend and multi-platform support for improving the computational flexibility and efficiency of metaheuristic optimization.

items.title: On the Cohomological Amplitude of the Locally Analytic Jacquet--Langlands Functor
items.summary: We prove a local cohomological bound $RΓ_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}(X,\mathcal F)\in D^{[0,\dim X]}$ for a pro-étale sheaf with a derived $p$-complete integral lattice whose modulo $p^m$ reductions are filtered colimits of finite local systems on an affinoid topologically of finite type over $C$. For $G=\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$, with $n\geq2$ and $F/\mathbb Q_p$ finite, we apply these local bounds to variants of Scholze's Jacquet--Langlands functor $\mathrm{JL}_\mathscr{B}(Π):= RΓ_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}(\mathbb{P}^{n-1}_C,\mathcal{F}_Π\otimes^{L, \square}_{\mathbb{Q}_p}\mathscr{B})$ for $\mathscr{B}\in\{\mathbb{Q}_p, \widehat{\mathscr{O}}, \mathbb{B}_J\}$ and Banach or compact-type LB representations $Π$ of $G$, obtaining $\mathrm{JL}_{\mathscr{B}}(Π)\in D^{[0,2(n-1)]}$ for each choice of $\mathscr{B}$. We also prove that for arbitrary continuous principal series $I(η)=(\mathrm{Ind}_B^Gη)^{\mathrm{cont}}$, we have $\mathrm{JL}(\mathrm{Ind}_B^Gη)\in D^{[0, n]}$, while $\mathrm{JL}_{\widehat{\mathscr{O}}}(I(η)),\mathrm{JL}_{\mathbb{B}_J}(I(η))\in D^{[0, n-1]}$.

items.title: Diophantine conditions for absolute continuity of projections for self-similar measures
items.summary: We prove that every projection of a planar self-similar measure $μ$ is equivalent to Lebesgue measure on its support if the rotations satisfy a simultaneous Diophantine condition with exponent $τ$ and $μ$ has finite $s$-energy for some $1+2τ\le s<2$. Under strong separation, we prove the fibre measures have exact dimension $\dim_Hμ-1$. For self-similar sets $E$ with $\dim_H E>1+2τ$, the same rotation condition implies uniformly positive projection lengths and fibres of dimension $\dim_H E-1$ at Lebesgue-almost every point of each image without separation assumptions. The absolute continuity and fibre dimension theorems extend to non-coordinate projections of products under a joint Diophantine condition with exponent $τ$ on the logarithmic contraction ratios. These imply for all self-similar sets $K,L\subset\mathbb R$ satisfying this condition and $\dim_HK+\dim_HL>1+2τ$, every sum $uK+L$, $u\ne 0$, has positive length, and $\dim_H(L\cap(y-uK))=\dim_HK+\dim_HL-1$ for Leb. a.e. $y\in uK+L$. The proof combines the $L^1$ Gaussian smoothing approach used in the higher dimensional case with averaging at random stopping scales with a Brownian martingale bound using Itô calculus.

items.title: Permutation symmetries and characteristic polynomials
items.summary: We compute certain multilinear functionals of permutation-invariant random matrices, following the work of Marcus and Geneson. As an application, we derive formulae for the average characteristic polynomial of the sum and the product of permutation-invariant random matrices.

items.title: The Paley--Wiener excess and a local law for the ${\rm Sine}_β$ process
items.summary: The main result of this paper is the proof that the Paley--Wiener excess of the ${\rm Sine}_β$ process almost surely equals $\lfloor \sqrt{2/β}\rfloor$ for all $β>0$. We also derive the loop equations for the resolvent of the ${\rm Sine}_β$ point process and use them to obtain accurate bounds on the moments of the associated Stieltjes transform.

items.title: Converse Lyapunov theorem for input-to-state stability of infinite-dimensional systems
items.summary: We prove converse Lyapunov theorems for input-to-state stability (ISS) of a broad class of infinite-dimensional systems applicable to evolution equations in Banach spaces, boundary control systems, and delay systems. To this end, we employ a novel method that does not require constructing auxiliary closed-loop systems. We start by showing that ISS of a control system implies uniform global asymptotic stability of the same system with respect to trajectory-dominated inputs. Then, under an additional regularity requirement, we prove that an ISS Lyapunov function can be constructed. Based on our general result, we prove that for linear systems with unbounded $\infty$-admissible operators, ISS is equivalent to the existence of a Lipschitz continuous coercive ISS Lyapunov function.

items.title: Imaginary Non-CM Fields of $2$-Power Degree
items.summary: We establish a new method for the study of imaginary non-CM fields of arbitrary \(2\)-power degree and class number one. In particular, we show that for degrees greater than \(16\), dihedral fields either lie in the ray class field of one of the three imaginary quadratic fields \(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-2})\), \(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3})\),\(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-19})\),\(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-43})\), \(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-67})\), whose conductor is supported only on primes dividing \(2\), with explicit upper bounds on the relevant exponents, or are Hilbert class fields of imaginary quadratic fields. We also give a complete classification of the \(161\) imaginary non-CM fields of degree \(16\) with class number one, providing explicit tables of defining polynomials, Galois groups, base fields, and conductors. These \(161\) non-CM fields, together with the six CM fields classified by Louboutin and Okazaki \cite{lou7}, complete the classification of all imaginary fields of degree \(16\) with class number one. For CM fields, the problem reduces to computing relative class numbers via analytic class number formulae, whereas for non-CM fields the absence of a totally real subfield of index \(2\) requires a different approach and leads to a richer variety of Galois groups and ramification patterns.

items.title: R-Function Representation and Composition for Flexibility Analysis and Robust Design Spaces
items.summary: Explicit multiparametric solutions provide analytical feasibility and design-space descriptions after elimination of adjustable variables. R-functions convert these descriptions into fields whose nonnegative regions represent feasible or robust designs. The principal contribution is the analytical composition of independently derived design spaces through union, intersection with engineering restrictions, and exclusion of prohibited regions, without repeating the underlying multiparametric elimination. A support-function construction supplies the robust design fields used in this composition. A two-parameter example demonstrates how alternative configurations, a manufacturing restriction and an exclusion combine into one admissible field. The resulting representations also support geometric interrogation of external boundaries, internal interfaces and limiting uncertainty contact, illustrated by a four-parameter heat-exchanger network. Explicit MPC offers a potential further application.

items.title: On the entire solutions of Schröder iteration functions of first and second kind
items.summary: Let $S_{f,n}$ and $K_{f,n}$ denote Schröder's methods of the first and second kind with given order $ n $ ($\geq 2 $) applied to an entire function $ f $. This article investigates the existence of the entire solutions $f$ whenever $ S_{f,n} $ and $ K_{f,n} $ are rational. Utilizing the Nevanlinna theory, we obtain the general form of entire solutions for such equations. It is proved that either of $ S_{f,n} $ and $ K_{f,n} $ is a non-identity rational map if and only if $f = p e^{q}$, for some polynomials $p$ and $q$. Additionally, we provide one recurrence relation of $K_{f,n}$ depending only upon $K_{f,n-1}$.

items.title: Intersection multiplicity of a sparse curve and a trinomial curve
items.summary: Let f $\in$ C[x, y] be a trinomial and let g $\in$ C[x, y] be a sparse polynomial with N monomials (N $\ge$ 1). We address the problem of bounding the local intersection multiplicity of the bivariate polynomial system f = g = 0 at an isolated root q $\in$ (C * )^ 2 only in terms of N . Our main result establishes that the local multiplicity of the system at any isolated solution q $\in$ (C * ) ^2 is at most (N -1)(N +2)/ 2 , independently of the degrees of f and g. Furthermore, we know that this bound is sharp for N = 3.

items.title: Rigidity does not imply substitution rigidity
items.summary: We obtain a negative answer to a question of Freudenburg concerning rigidity conditions for a polynomial. We construct a polynomial that does not lie in the kernel of any nonzero locally nilpotent derivation on the polynomial ring, but there exist an affine domain, algebraically independent elements and a locally nilpotent derivation such that the result of substituting elements into the polynomial lies in the kernel of that locally nilpotent derivation, but at least one of the substituted elements does not lie in that kernel.

items.title: Asymptotic stability of the 2D Boussinesq equations around Couette flow in infinite channel
items.summary: In this paper, we investigate the stability threshold of the two-dimensional Boussinesq system around the Couette flow in an infinite channel $\mathbb{R}\times[-1,1]$ under Navier-slip boundary condition. To address nonlinear echo chains induced by temperature-vorticity coupling, we construct a two-level frequency-dependent temporal decomposition, with the two levels matched to the infinite and finite superposition principles for the equation, respectively. By fully exploiting the enhanced dissipation effect at each decomposition level, we prove that if the initial perturbation $(ω^{in}, θ^{in})$ around the Couette flow satisfies $\|ω^{in}\|_{H^4_{x,y}\cap L^1_xH^4_y}\leq cν^{\frac{1}{3}}$, and $\|θ^{in}\|_{H^5_{x,y}\cap L^1_xH^5_y}\leq cν^{\frac{2}{3}+}$, the Boussinesq system admits a globally asymptotically stable solution. It should be emphasized that the method in this paper provides an effective approach for the hydrodynamic equations with coupling effects.

items.title: Representing the Non-dominated Set of Multi-objective Network Problems by Supported Non-dominated Points
items.summary: In multi-objective combinatorial optimization, unsupported non-dominated points typically outnumber supported points and are often significantly more challenging to compute. Recent studies show that extreme supported non-dominated points provide high-quality representations of the non-dominated set for certain binary problems. We demonstrate that this observation does not generalize to capacitated network optimization problems: representation quality decreases with increasing arc capacities, whereas supported non-dominated points consistently provide high-quality representations with respect to several quality indicators. However, supported point sets may still be too large in practical applications, where only a small, fixed number of alternatives is typically desired. Selecting fixed-size representations from the non-dominated set requires its computationally expensive generation and thus diminishes the computational advantages that representations are intended to provide. We therefore suggest the (extreme) supported points as alternative candidate sets in subset selection problems. Our numerical results show that restricting the candidate set to supported non-dominated points yields fixed-size representations of nearly the same quality as those selected from the complete non-dominated set. Overall, supported non-dominated points serve both as high-quality representations and as reasonable candidate sets for subset selection.

items.title: A Large Gap between Galerkin Errors with and without Mesh-Uniform Regularity for the KdV Equation with Boundary Dissipation
items.summary: We compare two cubic Hermite Galerkin semidiscretizations of the Korteweg-de Vries equation on a bounded interval with boundary dissipation. They use the same trial space. The first is the weighted scheme considered in our previous paper (arXiv:2610.39269), called the W-scheme. It has mesh-uniform regularity: the discrete semigroups of the linearized equation inherit Crandall-Pazy regularity and Kato smoothing, with bounds uniform in the mesh size $h$. The second is the standard Galerkin method in $L^2$, called the S-scheme. It has no mesh-uniform regularity. For the W-scheme, the full error and the ordering error converge at an algebraic rate in $h$, uniformly on $[t_0,\infty)$ times small balls of $L^2$ for any fixed $t_0>0$. They are bounded by $Ch^p\varepsilon$ and $Ch^p\varepsilon^2$, respectively, where $\varepsilon$ is the size of the datum and $p>0$. We prove that neither bound holds for the S-scheme by using exact high-frequency spurious eigenpairs of the S-scheme. The existence of such eigenpairs for fine meshes with at least 512 elements has a proof checked by Lean 4. Computations compare the two schemes on unit-norm data built from these eigenfunctions, on 512, 1024 and 2048 elements. The full error of the S-scheme stays at $4.6\times10^{-2}$. That of the W-scheme is at most $2.2\times10^{-9}$. The ordering error of the S-scheme stays at $9.6\times10^{-6}$. That of the W-scheme falls from $2.3\times10^{-9}$ to $1.4\times10^{-10}$. Their ratio grows from $4.2\times10^3$ to $6.6\times10^4$.

items.title: Interface-Preserving ${H}_\infty$ Model Reduction of Network Systems
items.summary: We study projection-based reduced-order models that exactly retain specified input and output interfaces. Admissible projections are characterized geometrically: the retained subspace must contain every input and output direction, which fixes the minimum order. The reduction error factors into input-coupling, internal-dynamics, and output-coupling systems, giving a submultiplicative ${H}_\infty$ bound; for positively dominated factors the ${H}_\infty$ error equals a dc gain computable from linear solves. Strict dissipativity certifies the stability of every orthogonal reduction, and a Hankel singular value bounds the optimum a posteriori. These results motivate sequential graph-coarsening heuristics for networks. On a 65,566-state chip thermal network, interface-preserving coarsening yields sparse, positive lumped models that are more accurate than Kron reduction of the same interface at every order, with far fewer edges; balanced truncation is more accurate but destroys the network structure.

items.title: Exact codegree Turán densities of even zycles
items.summary: We determine the exact codegree Turán density of the $3$-uniform zycle $Z_\ell$ for every even integer $\ell\ge 8$ with $3\nmid\ell$,showing that $γ(Z_\ell)=1/3$. More generally, we prove that $γ(Z_\ell)\le 1/3$ for all even $\ell\ge 8$. Our results partially answer a question of Piga and Schülke [Bull. Lond. Math. Soc. 58 (2026), e70348] concerning the sharpness of their upper bound of $1/2$.

items.title: The Higher-Dimensional Nitsche Conjecture: Sharp Bounds and Rigidity
items.summary: Let $n\ge3$ and let $h:\A(r,1)\to\A(R,1)\subset\mathbb R^n$ be an onto homeomorphism with harmonic coordinate functions. We prove the sharp Nitsche bound \[ R\le R_{n,+}(r):=\frac{nr}{n-1+r^n}, \] and, when $h$ interchanges the two ends, the strictly stronger sharp bound \[ R\le R_{n,-}(r):=\frac{nr^{n-1}}{1+(n-1)r^n}. \] In each case, equality holds only for the corresponding radial harmonic homeomorphism, up to an orthogonal transformation. Both bounds and their equality cases extend to bounded harmonic maps in every dimension $n\ge2$. This requires nonzero degree of $h/|h|$ on interior spheres, $|h|\ge R$, and the corresponding $L^2$ limits of the modulus at the two ends. In the plane, we also prove the nonzero-winding-number conjecture of Iwaniec--Kovalev--Onninen [\emph{J. Amer. Math. Soc.} \textbf{24} (2011), 345--373], without endpoint modulus conditions. We prove a sharp $L^1$ contraction theorem for vector measures associated with spherical couplings. The first marginal is uniform, while the second is unrestricted. For bounded nonnegative nondecreasing zonal kernels, the optimal constant is the degree-one multiplier. If the kernel is also strictly increasing, equality holds exactly for couplings supported on orthogonal graphs. This theorem is the main tool in the proofs of the annular bounds and their rigidity.

items.title: Nonlinear integral equations for stress-controlled rheology: Collocation methods for Volterra equations with functional kernels
items.summary: We present a class of numerical collocation methods to solve a typical inverse problem that arises in the stress-controlled rheology of complex fluids with pronounced history-dependent response, where the relation between stress and flow rate is given by an integral constitutive equation as the material law. We demonstrate the method by calculating the creep response of a nontrivial model of a shear-thinning viscoelastic fluid where a stress overshoot in rate-controlled startup flow leads to ``sudden yielding'' in stress-controlled creep. Our method is able to address the long-time behavior of the model, distinguishing the amorphous solid from the stress-induced yielded fluid, and from the in-between case of infinite deformation that never achieves a stationary shear rate (proper creep). To this end, we implement a method with flexible time-stepping, and prove uniqueness of the solution and convergence of the methods for a broad class of highly viscoelastic non-linear rheological laws in integral form.

items.title: Monetisation and Cost Function Scalarisation Cannot Guarantee Valid Multi-Criteria Decision-Making
items.summary: Monetary quantities are not preferences. Cost is an object-related system performance; value-for-money is an actor's subjective evaluation of it. Monetisation embeds trade-off information: its conversion coefficients express valuations and determine how heterogeneous performances compensate one another. Cost-benefit analysis, even net present value, yields quantities of money, not the preference value actors attribute to them. This creates a monetisation paradox. Cost enters a multi-criteria problem as one performance among several, but money is then elevated into the universal representation of all others, creating representational dominance. The problem collapses into a single-criterion one in which every performance acts only through its imposed monetary equivalent. Cost-function scalarisation does not resolve this by substituting points, normalised scores, losses, or penalties: these transformations and their weights fix preference directions, intensities, and trade-offs, so they are implicit preference models, yet are treated as technical constructs rather than measured and validated. A well-defined scalar optimum is therefore not necessarily a decision-valid multi-criteria outcome. Numerical commensurability does not establish preference commensurability. Decision validity requires heterogeneous performances to be transformed into actor preferences in a unified preference domain. Preference is relational and contextual, yet can be represented on an affine scale. Preference Function Modelling and the Linear Preference Space provide the commensurability required for valid aggregation. The decision criterion should thus maximise aggregated actor preference over the feasible and acceptable design-decision space, not monetised quantities or scalarised scores.

items.title: The singular Gaussian scaling limit for a tagged particle in the infinite-dimensional Dyson model at $β=2$
items.summary: We prove a logarithmic central limit theorem for a tagged particle in infinite-dimensional Dyson Brownian motion at inverse temperature $β=2$, starting from the sine$_2$ point process. The fluctuation is of order $\sqrt{\log t}$, which is subdiffusive and substantially slower than the polynomial fluctuations of classical short-range interacting particle systems, reflecting the rigidity induced by long-range logarithmic repulsion. We further identify the scaling limit as the singular Gaussian field corresponding to the zero-Hurst parameter, which provides a realisation of the singular Gaussian field as a scaling limit of a tagged particle raised by Dürr, Goldstein and Lebowitz (Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 38 (1985)).

items.title: Sectorial normalisation of one resonant biholomorphisms near a fixed point
items.summary: In this article, we study germs of biholomorphisms of $(\C^n,0)$, $n\geq 2$ fixing the origin, the linear part at which has all its eigenvalues on the unit circle. We prove the existence of a {\it sectorial} transformation to a polynomial normal form of a non-degenerate 1-resonant biholomorphism under a Diophantine condition. We also give their holomorphic classification. We show that the {\it sectorial} automorphisms of the polynomial normal form are {\it exponentially flat} perturbations of the identity. We deduce the Gevrey character of the formal normalizing transformation and we show how the Gevrey index depends on the Diophantine exponent.

items.title: A stochastic gradient algorithm for non-separable optimization with convergence guarantee
items.summary: We study smooth parameterized non-separable objectives of the form $\mathcal L(θ)=F(Y(θ))$, where a global operator couples the outputs of all training samples. We analyze two stochastic gradient constructions within this output-space framework: the ideal per-batch gradient $G$, obtained by row sampling of the full output gradient, and a cached surrogate $H$ for parameterized updates in which full-data quantities are expensive to evaluate. For uniformly sampled batches, the ideal estimator has a deterministic batch-size scaling and a second moment controlled by the full output gradient. Using this structure, we establish local high-probability confinement and convergence for fixed positive step sizes on a prescribed parameter neighborhood under a power-type gradient inequality, with linear and polynomial regimes determined by its exponent. For the cached surrogate, a Lyapunov function couples the objective gap with the cache error and yields analogous local results on the corresponding non-exit event. The theory includes explicit path-length, confinement, and rate bounds; numerical experiments illustrate finite-budget decay trends and the effects of global output-gradient sampling, batch restriction, and cache tracking.

items.title: Counting subalgebras of $\mathfrak{o}^n$
items.summary: Let $\mathfrak{o}$ be a compact discrete valuation ring with residue field $\mathbb{F}_q$. We study the cotype zeta function of finite-index subalgebras of $\mathfrak{o}^n$ by adapting an approach developed by Voll for more general algebras. For each $\emptyset\neq I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n-1\}$, we express the generating series counting subalgebras whose elementary divisor valuations, listed in decreasing order, have jumps precisely at the positions in $I$ as a finite weighted sum of $\mathfrak{o}$-adic integrals. We compute these integrals in several cases, obtaining explicit formulas for the generating series associated with every singleton set $I$ in arbitrary rank. We also obtain the cotype zeta function of unital subalgebras of $\mathfrak{o}^4$. As a by-product, we obtain a universal lower bound for the abscissa of convergence of the subalgebra zeta function of any $\mathfrak{o}$-algebra that is free of rank $n$ as an $\mathfrak{o}$-module. We also establish several results concerning the uniformity problem for the subalgebra zeta function of \(\mathfrak{o}^n\). To do so, we study two systems of polynomial equations over the residue field and apply the results to derive the number of irreducible unital subalgebras of $\mathfrak{o}^n$ of index $q^e$, for $e\leq n+3$. Finally, we use the decomposition of subalgebras into local factors to obtain the number of unital subalgebras of $\mathfrak{o}^n$ of index $q^e$ for $e\leq 9$. For each fixed $n$, these subalgebra counts are universal polynomials in $q$.

items.title: Differential Flatness of Nonlinear Consensus Networks: A Graph-Theoretic Perspective
items.summary: We study the property of differential flatness for networks of identical flat agents coupled through a consensus protocol, where a single exogenous input acts on one agent and the output of another agent is measured. We distinguish whether the network admits a flat output at all from whether the measured task output is a flat output. For the former, we show that flatness at a synchronized equilibrium requires controllability of the Laplacian leader--follower pair, which is also sufficient for linear agents but not for nonlinear ones. For the latter, we show that the relative degree of the task output is determined by its graph distance to the input node, so that it is a flat output if and only if the graph is a path with the input and output nodes at its ends. Numerical examples illustrate how flatness enables finite-time transitions between consensus configurations through a single input.

items.title: Completely monotone memory systems
items.summary: Linear time-invariant (LTI) relaxation systems are characterized by a completely monotone impulse response. This paper proposes an extension of this property to nonlinear systems: a system is said to have completely monotone memory if a positive increment in the past input leads to a completely monotone increment in the future output. We show that this property constitutes a strong form of monotonicity, while also imposing stability constraints that closely resemble fading memory, contraction, and incremental stability. We also show that completely monotone memory is equivalent to classical relaxation for LTI systems and to a combination of monotonicity and stability for a class of scalar state-affine systems. Finally, we illustrate the relevance of our framework to the gating dynamics of conductance-based models.

items.title: Gelfand and sampling numbers of weighted Wiener spaces
items.summary: The aim of this paper is to establish sharp asymptotic bounds on the Gelfand numbers of weighted Wiener spaces $\mathcal{A}^r_θ$ measured in $L_q$. This is done by using results for Gelfand numbers of sequence spaces and applying them to each layer of a hyperbolic cross to obtain results for Gelfand numbers between different (weighted) Wiener spaces. These can then be used to establish bounds in $L_q$ by combining them with known results and techniques for Besov spaces. This significantly narrows a gap in the current research, since the Gelfand numbers provide a lower bound on the (non-linear) sampling numbers, whereas upper bounds on this quantity have been studied in multiple papers via an upper bound given by the best m-term approximation.

items.title: Adaptive refinement in defeaturing problems via an equilibrated flux a posteriori error estimator
items.summary: An adaptive refinement strategy, based on an equilibrated flux a posteriori error estimator, is proposed in the context of defeaturing problems. Defeaturing consists of removing features from complex domains to simplify mesh generation and reduce the computational cost of simulations. It is a common procedure, for example, in computer aided design for simulation-based manufacturing. However, depending on the problem at hand, geometrical simplification may significantly deteriorate the accuracy of the solution. The proposed adaptive strategy is hence twofold: starting from a defeatured geometry, it iteratively performs both standard mesh refinement and geometrical refinement by selecting, at each step, which features must be reintroduced to significantly improve accuracy. Similar adaptive strategies have been previously developed using residual-based error estimators within an IGA framework. Here, instead, we extend a previously developed equilibrated flux a posteriori error analysis, designed for standard finite element discretizations, to make it fully applicable within the adaptive procedure. In particular, we address the assembly of the equilibrated flux estimator in presence of elements trimmed by the boundary of included features, adopting an unfitted finite element strategy to handle feature inclusion. The resulting estimator allows us to bound both the defeaturing and the numerical sources of error, with additional contributions accounting for the weak imposition of boundary conditions.

items.title: Degradation-Aware Participation of Battery Storage in Frequency Regulation Markets
items.summary: As data centers make the load on the power grid fluctuate faster, frequency regulation grows more valuable. Battery energy storage systems (BESSs) are well suited to provide frequency regulation, but providing this service speeds up aging, especially during operation at extreme state of charge (SoC). In the PJM interconnection, the grid operator supplies a regulation signal that a participating BESS is expected to follow, within a capacity that it must bid before the signal is known. Accordingly, we decompose the degradation-aware frequency regulation problem into a bidding layer and an operations layer. For bidding, we propose an adaptive strategy, assuming perfect tracking in which the bid depends on the SoC expected at the start of the bid period by means of choosing basepoints. For operation, the BESS further protects its battery by deliberately giving up a perfect performance score, to keep its SoC away from the extremes. On the PJM regulation signal and prices of 2023, adaptive bids lengthen the battery life by $31\%$ against bidding full capacity, for $2.2\%$ of the revenue. Giving up a perfect score in operation lengthens the battery life of constant bids by $10\%$ to $27\%$, at a change in revenue of at most $0.2\%$.

items.title: Renewable model averaging for generalized linear models
items.summary: Prediction is one of the most important research topics in statistics and machine learning. Moreover, in the domain of streaming data analysis, real-time prediction has become a rapidly growing research field in recent years, owing to the abundance of streaming data. In many fields of scientific research, such as biomedical research, weather forecasting, and traffic management, improving real-time prediction of streaming data is crucial in general. However, the complicated features of streaming data, such as large-scale and high-velocity, impose both theoretical and computational challenges to the development and evaluation of real-time prediction in this field, especially when the investigator has multiple models at hand. To overcome these challenges, we propose a novel Renewable Model Averaging method through Quadratic approximation (ReMAQ) for generalized linear model (GLM) for streaming data. By approximating the model averaging procedure for GLMs (which is typically a convex optimization problem) with a quadratic optimization formulation, ReMAQ allows us to update the model averaging prediction sequentially when a new batch of data arrives, without accessing the entire historical data. Moreover, ReMAQ is also computationally efficient as one only needs to consider a quadratic programming problem in each steps of updating. Under certain regular conditions, we also show that the proposed ReMAQ weight is asymptotically equivalent to that by the oracle model averaging based on the inaccessible full data, the asymptotic optimality of ReMAQ is then established accordingly. The proposed method is also assessed by simulation studies. We apply our proposed ReMAQ in the study of the Airline On-Time Performance Dataset and the results demonstrate the superiority our method in practical situations.

items.title: Optimal Actuator Support Design for Infinite-Horizon Linear-Quadratic Parabolic Control Problems
items.summary: We study an optimal actuator design problem for infinite-horizon LQ control problems governed by parabolic equations. The control acts only on a small measurable subregion of the spatial domain, and the objective combines the infinite-horizon control value with a cost for the actuator region. Using the Riccati representation of the value function, we derive a comparison identity for two actuator supports and obtain an exact expansion of the objective. This leads to a topological derivative with respect to local changes in the support. We prove a localized Riccati sensitivity estimate to control the remainder and show that the infinite-horizon term in the derivative can be computed by solving a Lyapunov equation. This yields a computable support-update algorithm with a measure-controlled Armijo search. Under explicit uniform remainder and admissibility assumptions, its first-order stationarity defect tends to zero. Numerical experiments illustrate these results.

items.title: Single-point determination of a potential and a nonlinearity in a semilinear biharmonic equation
items.summary: In this paper, we study the inverse problem of determining the coefficient $q$ and the nonlinearity $F$ in the semilinear biharmonic equation $Δ^2 u+q(x)u=F(x,u)$ with Navier boundary data. The measurement consists of $\partial_νu(x_0)$ at a fixed boundary point $x_0$. We apply the mixed variation approach to linearize the nonlinear problem and construct semiclassical boundary-localized solutions for the linearized equation. Under suitable analyticity, nonresonance, and nondegeneracy assumptions on $q$ and $F$, we prove that this boundary point measurement uniquely determines both $q$ and $F$. We also establish boundary determination of all normal derivatives of $q$ and of the first nonzero Taylor coefficient of $F$ on a nonempty relatively open subset of the boundary. When the linear potential $q$ is known, we prove that either component of the Navier boundary input alone suffices to determine $F$, and that the polynomial nonlinearity can be uniquely determined without requiring any analyticity conditions. For suitable finite-dimensional classes of nonanalytic potentials, we also obtain, for fixed $F$, the stable determination of $q$ from finitely many boundary inputs and the associated point measurements. In addition, as an important supplement, we provide nontrivial examples verifying the main assumptions, as well as counterexamples concerning the recovery of the linear coefficient. Finally, we present numerical experiments that demonstrate the theoretical results.

items.title: A Strict Upper Bound for Three-Point Weighted Selection in Planar Vector-Valued Regression
items.summary: We prove $F_{\mathrm{weighted}}(2,2,3)<11/6$ for minimum-Frobenius-norm least-squares regression with two input and two output coordinates, improving the upper bound $15/8$. More precisely, a universal $\varepsilon_0>0$ satisfies $\mathcal T_3\le(5/6-\varepsilon_0)E$ for every finite residual frame. The proof combines an exact scalar certificate, rigidity of equality in planar selection, and a compactness argument that controls disappearing weights. Together with the known lower bound, this gives $13/8\le F_{\mathrm{weighted}}(2,2,3)<11/6$. No numerical value of $\varepsilon_0$ is claimed.

items.title: The finite projective classification of complex spinors via momentum maps
items.summary: We describe the projective orbits of complex spinors from the point of view of the momentum map. We treat the irreducible spin modules in odd dimensions 1,3,5,7,9,11 and the half-spin modules in even dimensions 2,4,6,8,10,12,14, which are the only cases with finitely many orbits. In the Clifford--Fock model, we construct representatives as sums of pure basis spinors, and the coefficients are chosen so that the representative is a critical point of the squared norm of the momentum map. The resulting momentum values in a fixed Weyl chamber distinguish the orbits. Completeness follows from Vinberg's theory of graded Lie algebras and stabilizer actions, independently of the classical spinor classifications. We recover the classical counts of 1,1,1,2,3,5 orbits in the odd cases and 1,1,1,2,2,4,9 in the even cases, and compute the projective dimension of every orbit. In dimension fourteen we also determine the closure order of the orbits, using the fact that the minimum of the squared momentum norm increases strictly under degeneration.

items.title: The arithmetic de Rham stack
items.summary: We define and study the arithmetic de Rham stack $X^{\operatorname{arith}}$ of a scheme $X$ over a field of characteristic $p$, and analyze its relation with related stacks such as the Hyodo--Kato stack. We show that $X^{\operatorname{arith}}$ gives a stack-theoretic approach to rigid cohomology and its coefficients, known as overconvergent isocrystals and arithmetic $D$-modules, which avoids the long-standing problem of frame-choosing in earlier approaches. We finally give some arithmetic applications of our formalism, such as a proof of Berthelot's conjecture on the preservation of overconvergent isocrystals by smooth proper pushforward.

items.title: A SHARP MASS THRESHOLD FOR BOUNDEDNESS IN A CRITICAL QUASILINEAR CHEMOTAXIS MODEL WITH INDIRECT SIGNAL PRODUCTION: THE RADIALLY SYMMETRIC CASE
items.summary: A critical quasilinear chemotaxis model with indirect signal production in space dimensions higher than two is studied under radial symmetry. Exploiting the variational structure of the system, the existence of a sharp mass threshold M\textsubscr{c} > 0 is established: all solutions with mass below M\textsubscr{c} are global and bounded, while those with mass above M\textsubscr{c} and sufficiently negative energy are global but blow up in infinite time. Moreover, the value of the critical mass M\textsubscr{c} is related to the best constant of a variant of a Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality.

items.title: Learning inexact alternating minimization for convex problems with quadratic coupling
items.summary: Alternating minimization is a standard tool for optimization problems with two coupled variable blocks. Its cost is dominated by the inner subproblem solvers, which rarely have a closed-form solution. In this paper, we propose to learn an inexact alternating scheme in which neural networks approximate the subproblem solution at each iteration. For convex problems with quadratic couplings between the variable blocks that satisfy a quadratic growth condition, we derive a worst-case bound on the optimality gap that exposes the per-iteration error that each network is trained to minimize in a greedy fashion. Combining the bound with a PAC-Bayes argument, we obtain a fixed-horizon, high-probability bound on the expected optimality gap over the distribution of problem instances. We apply the learned scheme to robust matrix completion and low-dose CT reconstruction with dictionary regularization where we achieve a 5x-13x speedup over the inexact first-order baseline at matched accuracy. A brief end-to-end fine-tuning stage extends this up to 30x and outperforms other learned schemes. The code is available at https://github.com/paulhausner/learned-alternating-minimization.

items.title: Investigating parameter dependence for counterexamples to Payne's nodal line conjecture using HPC
items.summary: The behavior of the nodal line of the second eigenfunction of the negative Laplacian has been widely studied. Dahne could show numerically for one domain with six holes in two dimensions that it is possible to reject Payne's nodal line conjecture. We investigate the behavior of the nodal line if it does not touch the boundary, specifically the general shape, its prediction, its dependence on the parameters, and the numbers of holes. In this paper, we could address these issues numerically with a very efficient parallelized algorithm showing the rejection for various domains with six and five holes.

items.title: Independence of Hasse--Weil $L$-functions over rings of Dirichlet series
items.summary: We study linear and algebraic independence of Hasse--Weil $L$-functions of abelian varieties over $\mathbb{Q}$, with Dirichlet series as coefficients. For nonzero varieties that are pairwise non-isogenous over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, we prove that their $L$-functions with arbitrary Dirichlet twists, together with all their derivatives and $1$, are linearly independent when the coefficient series use only primes from a set of natural density zero. For untwisted $L$-functions, this independence is equivalent to the condition that the varieties are pairwise non-isogenous over $\mathbb{Q}$. If the individual monodromy groups are connected, the result for varieties that are pairwise non-isogenous over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ extends to larger coefficient rings: the prime supports of coefficients are unrestricted outside a prescribed set of positive upper natural density and meet it in a set of natural density zero. We also characterize algebraic independence of untwisted $L$-functions in terms of the multiplicities of the simple isogeny factors of the varieties. The proofs combine an arithmetic-function lemma of Kaczorowski--Molteni--Perelli with Frobenius density arguments and require no analytic continuation or automorphy.

items.title: Spare Strategy Analysis and Design for Mega Satellite Constellations Using Markov Chain
items.summary: This paper presents a Markov-chain-based method for the early-phase analysis and design of spare-management architectures for large-scale satellite constellations. To assess the long-run viability of such concepts of operations, satellite failure and replenishment processes are modeled as Markov chains and analyzed through their stationary solution. We reinvestigate an indirect spare strategy, modeled as a multi-echelon periodic-review reorder-point/order-quantity policy, in which spares are first delivered to parking orbits and then transferred to constellation planes. The stock levels in constellation and parking orbits are each modeled as independent Markov chains, and a fixed-point iteration yields a consistent joint stationary solution that describes the strategy's average behavior. This approach accurately captures the stochastic interplay within a multi-echelon model driven by orbital mechanics, avoiding the aggregation assumptions of prior works and remaining valid across a wider operating domain. Building on this fast, accurate analysis, we formulate an optimization problem and solve it via a genetic algorithm. Finally, we demonstrate the practical value of both the analysis method and the optimization framework in a real-world mega-constellation case study.

items.title: Scattering for the KP-II equation
items.summary: We prove scattering in $L^2(\mathbb R^2)$ for real-valued solutions of the Kadomtsev--Petviashvili II (KP-II) equation with localized initial data. The localization is measured in scale-invariant Lorentz or mixed Lebesgue spaces. The admissible data include all real-valued Schwartz functions. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first result establishing scattering for the KP-II equation for every real-valued Schwartz initial datum, without any smallness assumption and without the zero mean condition. We also show that some localization is necessary: there are smooth real-valued initial data of arbitrarily small $L^2$ norm, with a logarithmic moment, for which the solution does not scatter in $L^2$.

items.title: Singularising quantum channels preserving kappa-additivity
items.summary: We construct quantum channels by averaging unitary shift conjugations with respect to $κ$-additive probability measures on measurable abelian groups. The channels act on the duals of operator algebras generated by shifts and bounded measurable multiplication operators. They preserve $κ$-additivity of quantum states and admit a weak-$*$ integral representation on this class. If the averaging measure vanishes on singletons, every output state is singular. In the appendix, we also establish the corresponding Fubini's theorem for $κ$-additive measures.

items.title: Lie algebras graded by the root system $AG_2$
items.summary: We study Lie algebras graded by the generalized root system $AG_2$, which is obtained from $G_2$ by adjoining the doubles of its short roots, over fields of characteristic different from $2$ and $3$. We show that every such Lie algebra with a grading subalgebra of type $A_2$ is, modulo its center, the Tits-Kantor-Koecher Lie algebra of a structurable algebra equipped with an idempotent $t$ satisfying $t+\overline{t}=1$. Conversely, every structurable algebra with such an idempotent gives rise to an $(AG_2,A_2)$-graded Lie algebra. We describe the corresponding Peirce decomposition and characterize the additional algebraic structure required for an $(AG_2,G_2)$-grading. Using the classification of central simple structurable algebras, we determine the central simple examples when the characteristic is also different from $5$. Finally, we compare our constructions with the theory of Tits hexagons. For the central simple examples in which all root spaces are non-zero, we determine which ones are Tits-hexagonalizable; in certain cases, this imposes an additional balancing condition on the idempotent.

items.title: A phase transition for the cokernels of random band matrices over the p-adic integers
items.summary: Let $\mathbf{B}_n$ be an $n\times n$ Haar-uniform band matrix over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ with band width $w_n$. We prove that $\text{cok}(\mathbf{B}_n)$ has Cohen-Lenstra limiting distribution if and only if \[\lim_{n\to\infty} \left(w_n-\log_p(n)\right)=+\infty.\]

items.title: Exponential mixing for the randomized two-vortex model
items.summary: This paper investigates the mixing of passive scalars advected by a randomized two-vortex model on $\mathbb{T}^2$, in which the vortices interact through a regularized Biot--Savart kernel and are driven by independent Brownian motions. We establish quenched exponential mixing for the Lagrangian flow, characterized by the exponential correlation decay of mean-zero $H^s$ observables. The proof proceeds by establishing ergodicity of the associated two-point Markov process. We combine a uniform contraction estimate with controllability arguments to verify the Lyapunov drift and minorization conditions, allowing us to apply Harris-type theorem.

items.title: Weighted Recursions for Hurwitz Class Numbers
items.summary: We establish new recursions for Hurwitz class numbers with polynomial weights. In contrast to previous recursions, our results decouple class numbers of even and odd discriminants. Our main tool is the vector-valued holomorphic projection operator applied to mock modular forms. We invoke representation theory to connect the relevant spaces of vector-valued modular forms to spaces of classical new and old forms. We thereby leverage the vanishing of spaces of vector-valued cusp forms not available in the scalar case.

items.title: Some invariants of totally disconnected locally compact groups: cohomology and combinatorics
items.summary: The paper investigates two invariants for totally disconnected locally compact (t.d.l.c.) groups: the number of ends and the rational discrete cohomological dimension. Firstly, for a compactly generated t.d.l.c. group $G$, it is shown that its number of ends can be expressed in terms of the low-dimensional rational discrete cohomology of $G$, generalising a notable theorem by E. Specker to the t.d.l.c. setting. Secondly, we focus on a t.d.l.c. group $G$ acting under suitable conditions on a building $Δ$, showing that both the number of ends and the rational cohomological dimension of $G$ are related to those of the Weyl group associated to $Δ$. In special cases, we compare the rational discrete cohomological dimension of $G$ to its flat-rank, and in the appendix we provide examples for which these two invariants coincide. Finally, for t.d.l.c. groups with rational discrete cohomological dimension one that act properly and chamber-transitively on locally finite buildings, we explicitly construct a proper cocompact action on a tree out of the action on the building. All the results of independent interest in Coxeter theory have been included in the appendix.

items.title: Ternary quadratic genera and generalized Hurwitz class numbers via quaternion orders
items.summary: We classify the genera of primitive positive definite ternary quadratic forms in the extremal cases of Lehman's level and discriminant conditions. The genera are parametrized by their level, discriminant, and genus conductor, which also distinguishes local forms having the same isotropy. Using the correspondence with quaternion orders of level $(N_1,N_2)$, we express their weighted representation numbers and class numbers in terms of generalized modified Hurwitz class numbers. The formulas allow arbitrary admissible prime power exponents and include the additional genera obtained by Watson's transformation. As an application, we determine all $255$ one-class genera in these families and give an explicit representation formula for each. Of these formulas, $110$ concern nonsquarefree $N_1N_2$.

items.title: On some formality criteria for DG-Lie algebras
items.summary: We give some formality criteria for a differential graded Lie algebra to be formal. For instance, we show that a DG-Lie algebra L is formal if and only if the natural spectral sequence computing the Chevalley-Eilenberg cohomology H(L,L) degenerates at second page.

items.title: Timelike conjugate points in Lorentzian length spaces
items.summary: We study notions of conjugate points along timelike geodesics in the synthetic setting of Lorentzian (pre-)length spaces, inspired by earlier work for metric spaces by Shankar--Sormani. After preliminary considerations on convergence of timelike and causal geodesics, we introduce and compare one-sided, symmetric, unreachable and ultimate conjugate points along timelike geodesics. We show that all such notions are compatible with the usual one in the smooth (strongly causal) spacetime setting. As applications, we prove a timelike Rauch comparison theorem, as well as a result closely related to the recently established Lorentzian Cartan--Hadamard theorem by Erös--Gieger. In the appendix, we give a detailed treatment of the Fréchet distance on the space of non-stopping curves up to reparametrization, a technical tool used throughout the paper.

items.title: Probabilistic counting of labelled trees with prescribed vertical edge profile
items.summary: The vertical edge profile of a labelled plane tree $t$ is the collection of integers counting the number of oriented edges from label $i$ to label $j$ for every possible pairs of labels $(i, j)$. In a previous work by the second author, it was shown that a process constructed from the vertical edge profile forms a Markov chain for a wide class of models of random labelled plane trees where edge label increments are constrained to lie in $\{-1, 0, 1\}$. The purpose of this paper is twofold. First, we continue the study of Markov properties of the vertical edge profile. In particular, we derive general formulas for the transition kernel and the initial distribution of a class of Markov chains related to the vertical edge profile. Second, we apply these results to the probabilistic enumeration of trees with a prescribed vertical edge profile. These applications yield a unified probabilistic derivation of several enumeration formulas. In particular, we recover some results established Bousquet-Mélou and Chapuy for binary trees and Cayley trees. These enumeration formulas admit a remarkable factorized form, already noted in previous works. The probabilistic methods developed here explain this phenomenon by showing that these factorizations arise naturally from the Markov structure underlying the vertical edge profile.

items.title: Existence of a non-zero steady-state solution to a population density equation subject to horizontal transfer
items.summary: From plasmid dynamics and efflux pump expression in bacteria to risk-taking behaviour in human groups, horizontal interactions can drive the transmission of deleterious traits that spread despite carrying no selective advantage, thereby burdening the population. How can such detrimental traits persist, and under what conditions can the population avoid extinction? To address these questions, we model a population structured by a continuous trait representing individual burden within a non-linear, non-local integro-differential framework. From an analytical perspective, mutations are modeled via a jump operator rather than a diffusion term; consequently, the mutation operator lacks regularizing properties and is generally non-self-adjoint. Moreover, working in a weighted L 1 setting precludes the direct application of standard Krein-Rutman theory. To overcome these hurdles, we construct a custom fixed-point operator by first freezing the non-linearities to solve an auxiliary eigenvalue problem, and then tuning the resulting principal eigenvalue. Applying the Leray-Schauder fixed-point theorem to this operator rigorously yields the existence of a non-trivial steady state. Finally, numerical simulations illustrate the qualitative dynamics of the model and delineate the parameter regimes governing population persistence and extinction.

items.title: Generalized $\mathbb{Z}_p$ toric codes as qudit low-density parity-check codes
