items.summary: We study two-dimensional translation-invariant CSS stabilizer codes over prime-dimensional qudits on the square lattice under twisted boundary conditions, generalizing the Kitaev $\mathbb{Z}_p$ toric code by augmenting each stabilizer with two additional qudits. Using the Laurent-polynomial formalism, we adapt the Gröbner basis to compute the logical dimension $k$ efficiently, without explicitly constructing large parity-check matrices. We then perform a systematic search over various stabilizer realizations and lattice geometries for $p\in\{3,5,7,11\}$, identifying qudit low-density parity-check codes with the optimal finite-size performance. Representative examples include $[[242,10, \leq 22]]_3$ and $[[120,6, \leq 20]]_{11}$, both achieving $k d^{2}/n \leq 20$. Across the searched regime, the best observed $k d^{2}$ at fixed $n$ increases with $p$, with an empirical relation $k d^{2} = 0.0541 \, n^{2}\ln p + 3.84 \, n$, compatible with a Bravyi--Poulin--Terhal-type tradeoff when the interaction range grows with system size.

items.title: Rationally Null-homologous Floer Simple Knot
items.summary: We prove that every rationally null-homologous Floer simple knot in a closed, oriented, irreducible three-manifold with nonzero Thurston norm is unknotted. The proof combines a cut-and-reglue comparison for extremal Floer groups with Binns's theorem on Floer-minimal knots in balanced sutured manifolds.

items.title: Chvátal's Toughness Conjecture for Dense Almost Regular Graphs
items.summary: Chvátal's toughness conjecture asserts that there is a constant $t_0$ such that every $t_0$-tough graph on at least three vertices is Hamiltonian. Most partial results on this conjecture concern graphs with a restricted structure, such as chordal graphs and $H$-free graphs for small linear forests $H$. We confirm the conjecture with $t_0=4$ for dense almost regular graphs, without any structural assumption: for every $α>0$, there exist $\varepsilon>0$ and $n_0$ such that every $4$-tough graph $G$ on $n\ge n_0$ vertices with $δ(G)\geαn$ and $Δ(G)-δ(G)\le\varepsilon n$ is Hamiltonian. This result also bears on a conjecture of Bollobás and, independently, Häggkvist from the 1970s that every $k$-connected $D$-regular graph on $n$ vertices with $D\ge n/(k+1)$ is Hamiltonian. This conjecture is false for every $k\ge4$, even for large $n$. Our result shows that its conclusion holds for all large $n$ when $k$-connectivity is replaced by $4$-toughness, and that the degree condition can then be weakened to $D\geαn$ for an arbitrarily small fixed $α>0$. We also construct $3/2$-tough regular non-Hamiltonian graphs of linear degree, showing that the constant $4$ cannot be replaced by $3/2$.

items.title: The space of Dimension functions on a $C^*$-algebra
items.summary: In this paper, we prove that the space of normalized dimension functions on a unital $C^*$-algebra is either empty or a Choquet simplex. As a byproduct, we show that $W(A)$ is hereditary in $\operatorname{Cu}(A)$ for every $C^*$-algebra $A$. The argument combines an exact factorization for Cuntz comparison with Birkhoff's decomposition of lattice valuations. Moreover, we show that the space of normalized rank functions on a unital ring is either empty or a Choquet simplex.

items.title: Some examples of DG-Lie formality transfer
items.summary: We give a convenient reformulation, a slight generalization and some applications of the formality transfer theorem for DG-Lie algebras.

items.title: Linear Functional Estimation under Multiplicative Measurement Error with Unknown Error Distribution
items.summary: In this work we consider i.i.d. observations from a multiplicative deconvolution model, i.e. generated by $Y= X\varepsilon$, where $X$ and $\varepsilon$ are independent strictly positive random variables. The goal is to statistically infer the unknown signal $X$. Starting from the scenario where the probability density $f_\varepsilon$ of the error is known, we revisit local estimation strategies for several quantities of interest including the probability density function f and the survival function $S^X$ of the signal $X$. We use these results to propose a thresholded plug-in estimation technique for linear functionals in situations where the distribution of the error $\varepsilon$ is unknown, while having some additional data at our disposal. This estimation procedure combines the reconstruction of the unknown Mellin transform of $f$ as well as its regularized inversion by a spectral cut-off. We establish oracle-type upper bounds and discuss rates of convergence in explicit scenarios including estimating $f$ and $S^X$ pointwise. In addition, we develop a fully data-driven choice of the cut-off parameter via model selection, which is able to obtain the oracle risk up to a constant without any previous knowledge of the error distribution. The results are illustrated in a simulation experiment, where we compare different classes of distributions in settings with known and unknown $f_\varepsilon$.

items.title: High-order augmented Lagrangian methods and robust multilevel inner solvers
items.summary: We analyze high-order augmented Lagrangian methods for convex optimization problems with linear constraints and construct robust multilevel inner solvers. For the high-order proximal point method, we derive energy error estimates under uniform convexity that distinguish the sublinear, linear, and superlinear regimes by comparing the regularization power with the uniform convexity exponent. Through duality, these estimates yield convergence results for the high-order augmented Lagrangian method. The primal subproblems become nearly semicoercive as the penalty parameter decreases. We address this difficulty using multilevel subspace correction methods whose subspaces decompose the constraint kernel. Applications to nonlinear diffusion, Darcy--Forchheimer flow, and the finite neuron method show how the multilevel design accommodates mean, divergence, and boundary constraints. Numerical experiments illustrate the outer convergence regimes and demonstrate parameter-robust behavior of the inner solvers across different meshes.

items.title: Exponential Lower Bounds for Horn Amalgamation
items.summary: The amalgamation decision problem asks whether the finite models of a given universal first-order sentence have the amalgamation property. We prove that this problem is ExpTime-hard for universal Horn sentences of maximum relation arity three, and 2ExpTime-hard when the arity is unbounded, thereby strengthening the previous best lower bounds for universal Horn sentences. The first reduction simulates runs of nondeterministic tree automata using a single ternary relation and unary and binary auxiliary relations. The second simulates finite winning strategies in an exponential corridor game. As a secondary contribution, we prove that deciding the winner remains 2ExpTime-complete for the game normal form used in our reduction, in which each move label determines a unique legal successor from every non-winning legal row.

items.title: Gaps in the Most Frequent Sizes of Integer Sumsets
items.summary: Nathanson observed that, for four-element sets $A$ of integers, the most frequent sizes of the iterated sumset $hA$ are separated by triangular numbers. Senger proved this and suggested an analogue for larger sets. We establish this pattern for $k$-element subsets of $\{1,\ldots,q\}$, for every fixed $k\geq3$, where $h\geq2$ is either fixed or grows slower than $q^{1/(2k-1)}$. As $q\to\infty$, almost every such set has the largest possible $h$-fold sumset, and almost every exception has one of $h-1$ explicit smaller sizes. The differences between consecutive sizes among these $h$ values are consecutive $(k-2)$-dimensional simplex numbers.

items.title: Non-connected minimal clusters of small volume in a compact Finsler manifold
items.summary: We prove that isoperimetric clusters in general Finsler manifolds can be disconnected even when the volume constraint is small. This is in contrast with the Riemannian case and the ``fixed-norm'' case, where connectedness for arbitrarily small volume has recently been proved.

items.title: An approximation for solutions to Helmholtz equation in polygons and its application in learning based numerical method
items.summary: A learning based method for Helmholtz equations was proposed in [J. Comput. Phys. 520:113478,2025]. Based on Runge's approximation, it can be proved that when the solution can be continued outside the computational domain, using fundamental solutions as learning samples is sufficient to obtain the solution mapping with spectral accuracy. However, for complex geometries, such as domains with corners, approximation by fundamental solutions may only have logarithmic convergence due to the regularity issue, which is computationally impracticable. Moreover, approximation of a solution to the elliptic equation with those on larger domains is an ill-posed problem. In this work, we investigate how to feed additional learning samples to essentially get a practicable convergence rate and a stable algorithm, so as to ensure the generalizability of the learning based method. Error analysis and numerical examples illustrate flexibility and high-accuracy features.

items.title: Projections between Ramsey quasi-orders and topological Ramsey spaces
items.summary: A Ramsey quasi-order is a quasi-order $(\cal{R},\leq)$ such that $\cal{R}$ is a Polish space, $\leq$ is analytic and every analytic subset of $\cal{R}$ is Ramsey. In this paper, we study the transfer of the analytic Ramsey property via monotone quasi-open maps, which are closely related to a family of forcing projections between quasi-orders (ranging from weak projections to strong projections). We apply this framework to the class of topological Ramsey spaces by providing a detailed list of examples of strong projections between topological Ramsey spaces, and show that, for many of these examples, there is no weak projection in the reverse direction. We also exhibit pairs of topological Ramsey spaces that do not weakly project into each other. Finally, partially confirming a conjecture of Dobrinen, we show that every space in a large class of topological Ramsey spaces either strongly projects into the Ellentuck space or contains a dense set of atoms.

items.title: Fitting Gaussian vectors in normed spaces
items.summary: Given a family of $N$ i.i.d. Gaussian points in a $d$-dimensional normed space, what is the probability that some linear transformation maps it to the unit sphere? The case of a Euclidean space is known as the ellipsoid fitting problem and has recently attracted major attention. We initiate a study of this fitting problem in a general normed space, both asymptotically and in a fixed dimension. We specifically focus on the space $\ell_\infty^d$, where a combinatorial reformulation allows us to show that $cd^2/\log d$ points can be fitted with high probability. We illustrate that the geometry of the normed space is reflected in the fitting problem by showing that in dimension $2$, the spaces $\ell_2^2$ and $\ell_\infty^2$ are characterized by having extremal fittability properties.

items.title: Preference-Based Constraint Handling for Multi-Objective Design-Decision Optimisation: Acceptability Relaxation and Feasibility Guidance
items.summary: Multi-objective design-decision optimisation (MODO) problems contain negotiable acceptability limits and non-negotiable feasibility constraints. Hard constraints define the feasible design space, whereas actors may reconsider acceptability limits through deliberation and compromise. Relaxing such limits is a preference judgement: penalties or violation measures do not necessarily represent how actors value departures from initial requirements. This paper introduces a preference-based constraint-handling framework. For negotiable limits, preference functions model how actor preference changes with relaxation, allowing the preferred design and acceptable degree of relaxation to be determined through the same aggregation process. Approach 1 represents relaxation as an additional objective and search variable; Approach 2 incorporates it into the preference function of the affected criterion. When constructed consistently, both yield the same best-fit-for-common-purpose solution but differ in complexity and computational effort. The framework addresses stalemate problems, where relaxation is required to recover an acceptable solution, and non-stalemate problems, where modest relaxation may reveal a better design. Hard feasibility constraints remain fixed, and infeasible designs remain inadmissible. A feasibility-guidance function supplies IMAP-IGS with graded information on scaled violations, guiding the search towards difficult-to-reach feasible regions. Every feasible design takes precedence over every infeasible design, and the final recommendation is selected exclusively from the feasible set through A-FINE preference aggregation. The framework integrates acceptability negotiation, feasibility guidance, and design optimisation without conflating their meanings, while preserving preference consistency and decision validity.

items.title: Vanishing Control Times for Single-Input Bilinear Quantum Systems under Rapid Drift Spectral Growth
items.summary: This paper investigates the asymptotic behavior, as the Hilbert space dimension tends to infinity, of the state-to-state control time of single-input bilinear quantum systems whose control operator is drawn from an isotropic (unitarily invariant) random ensemble. Relying on deterministic graph-theoretic bounds, namely star cuts of the interaction graph for the lower bound and spanning trees for the upper bound, and on integration over the Haar measure, we derive high-probability lower and upper bounds on the control time, expressed in terms of the empirical spectral variance and of the relative concentration of the drift spectrum. Whenever the spectrum grows fast enough (for instance polynomially with an exponent larger than 3/2, geometrically, or super-exponentially), the upper bound vanishes and the control time tends to zero in probability: in these cases, enlarging the Hilbert space constructively speeds up control.

items.title: Horizontal estimates for Kloosterman sums under Hecke eigenvalue constraints
items.summary: We prove weighted cancellation under small-value conditions on Hecke eigenvalues of finitely many non-CM holomorphic newforms. We also obtain many squarefree integers of each sign with fixed normalized amplitude, simultaneously small Hecke eigenvalues, and a fixed bound on the number of prime factors, uniformly in growing reduced residue classes. Our questions are motivated by Xi's noncorrelation conjectures and the mixed-moment estimates of Jiang and Lau. Their estimates imply that small Hecke eigenvalues can occur together with non-small Kloosterman values. Our result retains this property with a fixed prime-factor bound, both signs, and the residue conditions. Using OpenAI's zero-free half-plane theorem for Dirichlet $L$-functions, we give an example with at most $83$ prime factors, normalized amplitude at least $10^{-21}$, and moduli $M\le C^{11/200}$.

items.title: Dynamic Topological Completeness for $\mathbb R^2$
items.summary: Dynamic topological logic (${\bf DTL}$) combines topological and temporal modalities to express asymptotic properties of dynamic systems on topological spaces. A dynamic topological model is a triple $\left <X,f,V\right >$, where $X$ is a topological space, $f:X\to X$ a continuous function and $V$ a truth valuation assigning subsets of $X$ to propositional variables. Valid formulas are those that are true in every model, independently of $X$ or $f$. A natural problem that arises is to identify the logics obtained on familiar spaces, such as $\mathbb R^n$. Slavnov showed that any satisfiable formula could be satisfied in some $\mathbb R^n$ for $n$ large enough, but the question of how the logic varies with $n$ remained open. In this paper we prove that any fragment of ${\bf DTL}$ that is complete for locally finite Kripke frames is complete for $\mathbb R^2$. This includes ${\bf DTL}^\bigcirc$; it also includes some larger fragments, such as ${\bf DTL_1}$, where ``henceforth" may not appear in the scope of a topological operator. We show that satisfiability of any formula of our language in a locally finite Kripke frame implies satisfiability in $\mathbb R^2$ by constructing continuous, open maps from the plane into arbitrary locally finite Kripke frames, which give us a type of bisimulation. We also show that the results cannot be extended to arbitrary formulas of ${\bf DTL}$ by exhibiting a formula which is valid in $\mathbb R^2$ but not in arbitrary topological spaces.

items.title: Fixed-occurrence cases of the shuffle-word-embedding conjecture
items.summary: For self-adjoint contractions in a finite tracial von Neumann algebra, binary shuffle traces with $m=1,2,4$ occurrences of the second variable admit simultaneous finite-dimensional approximation by commuting diagonal contractions. For every odd $m$, a commuting diagonal self-adjoint pair reproduces any prescribed finite set of shuffle traces exactly. When the first operator has finite spectrum and $m\geq3$ is odd, a weighted symmetric cycle reproduces all degrees simultaneously. We prove fourth-order trace-derivative positivity in finite tracial von Neumann algebras and obtain a positive measure representing the four-occurrence coefficients. For each even $m$, we characterize the contraction model property by positivity of an associated trace-derivative functional.

items.title: Quantitative stability of classical, entropic, and doubly entropic Wasserstein barycenters
items.summary: In this paper, we show how the recent analysis of (sharp) strong convexity properties of the Kantorovich functional by the third author can be used to establish new global quantitative stability estimates for Wasserstein barycenters and their entropic regularizations with respect to perturbations of the population distribution. For classical Wasserstein barycenters, we improve the state-of-the-art Hölder continuity exponent with respect to the $\mathcal{W}_1$ metric from $1/6$ to $1/4$, while drastically weakening the assumptions on the population distribution. We also provide an example which shows that the exponent $1/4$ cannot be improved. Motivated by computational considerations, we also analyze regularizations of Wasserstein barycenters with \emph{outer} and \emph{inner} entropic penalizations. For outer entropic barycenters, we establish novel higher-order stability results and in particular give a quantitative bound on relative Fisher information. Another contribution of our paper is a strong convexity estimate for an entropic version of the Kantorovich functional via soft Legendre transforms, enabling us to extend our stability results to \emph{doubly} entropic barycenters, as introduced by Chizat.

items.title: On definable closure in closed $H$-fields
items.summary: The definable closure of a real closed $H$-field $H$ in an ambient closed $H$-field extension $M$ is shown to be an immediate extension of $H$, except in two very special cases, where this is only true after adjunction to $H$ of a particular $H$-definable element of $M$ and then taking the real closure in $M$.

items.title: Towards Optimal Passive Feedback Control of LTI Systems under LQR Performance
items.summary: We study state-feedback design for continuous-time LTI systems with a control input and an external input-output pair. Our objective is to determine feedback gains that render the closed-loop system (strictly) passive with respect to the external port while minimizing the standard LQR cost in the disturbance-free case. The resulting constrained optimization problem is intractable due to bilinear matrix inequalities. We analyze the set of passivating gains, showing it is unbounded, possibly nonconvex, path-connected, and contractible. We propose an indirect approach, in which the set of passivating feedback gains is inner-approximated by a compact, convex polytope. A projected gradient flow is employed to compute a gain within this polytope that minimizes the LQR cost. Numerical examples illustrate the effectiveness of the method.

items.title: Global-dimension spectra of gentle algebras
items.summary: We classify the connected finite-dimensional gentle algebras of finite global dimension whose global-dimension spectra under derived equivalence are not intervals of integers. These are precisely the algebras with AAG invariant $[(2,4g)]$, where $g\geq2$, whose canonical line field is induced by a nowhere-vanishing vector field. Their spectrum is $\{2g,2g+2,\ldots,4g\}$. For each $g\geq2$, there are exactly two such derived-equivalence classes, distinguished by their Arf invariant. The geometric foundation is a realisation theorem for prescribed polygon weights in arbitrary genus. For an AAG invariant $[(m_i,n_i)]_{i=1}^b$ arising from such an algebra, the global dimensions attained in its AAG fibre form the integer interval $[\max_i\lceil n_i/m_i\rceil,\max_i n_i]$. By controlling the complete line-field invariant through local ribbon-graph constructions, we determine the spectrum in every derived-equivalence class.

items.title: Semisimple Deformations of Contraction Algebras for Smooth Threefold Flops
items.summary: Building on Bryan--Katz--Leung, Hua--Toda and Kawamata, we study deformations of contraction algebras and the local geometry of the scheme of associative algebra laws. Let $A$ be the basic contraction algebra of a completed projective flopping contraction of a smooth complex threefold. We construct a finite free polynomial family that is constant and semisimple away from the origin, with the original curve projectors fixed. For each restricted positive root $β=(β_i)$, with coordinates indexed by the retained vertices, the split generic fibre has $n_β$ matrix blocks of size $\sum_iβ_i$, and the labelled projector $e_i$ has rank $β_i$ on each block. Here $n_β$ is the corresponding genus-zero Gopakumar--Vafa invariant. If the geometric generic fibre of a finite free associative formal deformation of $A$ is semisimple, it has the same matrix factors, and any lifts of the original projectors have the same ranks on those factors. The scheme of associative algebra laws is smooth at $A$. The closure of the corresponding semisimple orbit is its unique irreducible component through $A$. The proof uses the curve divisors of Katz--Morrison and Nabijou--Wemyss, presentations of the universal contraction quotient and its cocenter, and the orbit method of Jelisiejew--Smoktunowicz. These presentations prove the geometric Hua--Toda flatness assertions. In the geometric families considered here, the relative contraction algebra, its centre and its cocenter are finite free over arbitrary complete Noetherian local complex bases. On a smooth open neighbourhood of $A$ in the scheme of algebra laws, the centres and cocenters form dual vector bundles compatible with arbitrary base change. For the type $D$ algebras $D_{n,2}$ with $n\ge2$, the centre morphism gives counterexamples to the smoothness assertion in Conjecture 1.4(2) of Jelisiejew--Smoktunowicz.

items.title: Microlocal properties of Cauchy evolution under metric variations
items.summary: We develop the microlocal analysis of the Cauchy evolution for wave-type equations on the infinite-dimensional space of Lorentzian metrics. We regard the Cauchy evolution operator as a distributional function of the metric, and give this notion a precise meaning through restrictions to finite-dimensional families of metrics. We study the singularities of this metric dependence. For normally hyperbolic operators on vector bundles, we determine the resulting operator-valued wavefront sets. Their parameter covectors are given by integrals of metric variations along individual null geodesics. At ultrastatic ends, metric dependence also determines the time-translation generators and their positive- and negative-energy splitting. More generally, the parameter singularities distinguish the two characteristic sheets and can be used to reconstruct the ordinary Cauchy propagation relation, which describes propagation of singularities. Consequences include smoothing under parameter averaging and polar-cone bounds associated with averaged null-positive variations, linking the result to averaged null energy conditions. The analysis also covers the Cauchy evolution of the Dirac equation.

items.title: Fujita exponents beyond integrable forcing
items.summary: We develop a unified framework for Fujita-type blow-up of solutions to the inhomogeneous semilinear heat equation $$\partial_tu-Δu=|u|^p+\mathbf{w}(x), \qquad (t,x)\in(0,\infty)\times\mathbb{R}^N, \qquad u(0, \cdot)=u_0.$$ The classical integrability assumptions on the forcing term are replaced by quantitative regular variation properties of its spatial mass $$F(R)=\int\limits_{|x|\le R}\mathbf{w}(x)\,dx.$$ Using techniques from regular variation theory together with the Mitidieri--Pohozaev test-function method, we establish sharp Fujita-type nonexistence results and identify the critical exponent in terms of the variation index of $F$. We prove that global solutions do not exist in the subcritical range and obtain critical-case blow-up under suitable slowly varying corrections. The regular variation framework further shows the optimality of the underlying mass condition, extends naturally to anisotropic settings through operator regular variation, and yields sufficient blow-up criteria for sign-changing forcings via the Gaussian-Laplace transform. The approach also applies to space-time dependent forcings, Riesz-potential type forcings, and equations involving the fractional Laplacian, providing a unified description of blow-up thresholds beyond the classical Fujita theory.

items.title: Geometry of multidimensional Farey summation algorithm and frieze patterns
items.summary: In this paper we develop a new geometric approach to subtractive continued fraction algorithms in high dimensions. We adapt a version of Farey summation to the geometric techniques proposed by F. Klein in 1895. More specifically we introduce Farey polyhedra and their sails that generalise respectively Klein polyhedra and their sails, and show similar duality properties of the Farey sail integer invariants. The construction of Farey sails is based on the multidimensional generalisation of the Farey tessellation provided by a modification of the continued fraction algorithm introduced by R. W. J. Meester. We classify Farey polyhedra in the combinatorial terms of prismatic diagrams. Prismatic diagrams extend boat polygons introduced by S. Morier-Genoud and V. Ovsienko in the two-dimensional case. As one of the applications of the new theory we get a multidimensional version of Conway-Coxeter frieze patterns. We show that multidimensional frieze patterns satisfy generalised Ptolemy relations.

items.title: The full length of short pants
items.summary: Bers proved that any genus $g$ hyperbolic surface admits a pants decomposition of length bounded above by a function of its genus. The goal here is to provide an explicit upper bound for the sums of lengths which is on the order of $(g \log(g)) ^{3/2}$.

items.title: Dualities and completions of median algebras and semilattices: a universal-algebraic approach
items.summary: We show that universal algebra, and the theory of natural dualities in particular, provides a uniform framework for the dualities between median algebras and bounded poc sets and their Boolean topological variants. We identify the Roller compactification of a CAT(0) cube complex with the profinite completion and the natural extension of the median algebra of its vertices. We then develop the order-theoretic perspective, which leads to a characterization of the profinite completion by the property that its intervals are the canonical extensions of the original ones. Since the basepoint orders of a median algebra have no top in general, we introduce conditional canonical extensions, show that they are unique, and realize them inside the profinite completion. Finally, a transfer theorem carries universal sentences from the finite quotients of a median algebra to its profinite completion, and we close with open questions on a correspondence theory between median algebras and their bounded poc sets.

items.title: Integer factorization as subset-sum problem
items.summary: This paper elaborates on a sieving technique that has first been applied in 2018 for improving bounds on deterministic integer factorization. We will generalize the sieve in order to obtain a polynomial-time reduction from integer factorization to a specific instance of the multiple-choice subset-sum problem. As an application, we will improve upon special purpose factorization algorithms for integers composed of divisors with small difference. In particular, we will refine the runtime complexity of Fermat's factorization algorithm by a large subexponential factor. Our first procedure is deterministic, rigorous, easy to implement and has negligible space complexity. Our second procedure is heuristically faster than the first, but has non-negligible space complexity.

items.title: Phase transition for the smallest eigenvalue of high-dimensional sample correlation matrices
items.summary: We study the smallest nonzero eigenvalue of the sample correlation matrix $\mathbf{R}_n$ formed from a $p_n \times n$ data matrix with i.i.d. real entries $ξ$ of mean zero and unit variance, in the high-dimensional regime $p_n / n \to φ\in (0, \infty) \setminus \{1\}$. In the tall regime $φ> 1$, we prove almost-sure convergence of $λ_n (\mathbf{R}_n)$ to the lower Marčenko--Pastur edge $λ_- = (1 - \sqrtφ)^2$ without additional moment assumptions. In the wide regime $φ< 1$, we establish a phase transition at the third-order tail scale. If $t^3 \mathbb{P}\{\lvert ξ\rvert > t\} \to 0$ as $t \to \infty$, the smallest eigenvalue $λ_{p_n} (\mathbf{R}_n)$ converges in probability to $λ_-$. While if $t^3 \mathbb{P}\{\lvert ξ\rvert > t\} \to \infty$, then $λ_{p_n} (\mathbf{R}_n)$ converges in probability to zero. At the critical scale $t^3 \mathbb{P}\{\lvert ξ\rvert > t\} \to κ\in (0, \infty)$, the point process of eigenvalues in the lower gap $(0, λ_-)$ converges in distribution to a Poisson random measure with explicit intensity. In this critical regime, we also identify the nondegenerate limiting distribution of $λ_{p_n} (\mathbf{R}_n)$, which has a continuous density on $(0, λ_-)$ and a positive atom at $λ_-$.

items.title: A Non-Dichotomy for CSPs of Stable $ω$-Categorical Structures
items.summary: We construct countable, stable, $ω$-categorical structures with at most two binary relations whose CSPs exhibit three complexity regimes: NP-complete, decidable but not in NP, and undecidable. The templates arise from a controlled Hrushovski construction of stable $ω$-categorical graphs $M_α$ for suitable irrational parameters $α>1$. Some of these graphs have NP-complete CSPs. Expanding the graphs $M_α$ by the non-edge relation turns age membership into a restriction of the CSP. For every time-constructible bound $t$, there is such an expansion whose CSP is decidable but not in DTIME$(t)$. For an explicit parameter $α$, the restriction to complete instances belongs to $\mathrm{coNP}$ and the full CSP belongs to $Σ_2^{\mathrm P}$. Separating the ages of the $M_α$ using graphs with large girth and prescribed density yields $2^{\aleph_0}$ distinct CSPs of these expansions, all but countably many of which are undecidable.

items.title: Sets of reach $R$ are $\operatorname{CAT}\left( 1/R^2\right)$
items.summary: Positive reach underpins many results in computational geometry and topology. It is used for triangulation criteria, topological inference, and manifold learning. The geometric properties of these sets have therefore been studied intensely. In this paper we focus on the intrinsic metric properties of sets of positive reach. In particular we give an elementary proof of the fact that (closed) sets of reach at least $R$ are $\operatorname{CAT}(1/R^2)$. This fact was established earlier by Alexander and Bishop, using quite significant machinery. The fact that a space is $\operatorname{CAT}(1/R^2)$ offers many advantages, such as the uniqueness and continuity of sufficiently short geodesics, the existence of Fr{é}chet means and by extension the Rips based homotopy reconstruction of Hausmann is available.

items.title: An asymptotic formula for primes of the form $u^2+v^2+1$
items.summary: We prove Motohashi's conjecture on primes of the form $u^2+v^2+1$, with Iwaniec's corrected constant. Let $b$ denote the characteristic function of the positive integers representable as a sum of two squares. Then, as $x\to\infty$, \[ \sum_{p\le x}b(p-1) =κ\Spr\frac{x}{(\log x)^{3/2}} +O\!\left(\frac{x}{(\log x)^{3/2}\sqrt{\log\log x}}\right), \] where $κ$ is the Landau--Ramanujan constant and $\Spr=\prod_{p\equiv3\,({\rm mod}\,4)}\bigl(1-1/(p(p-1))\bigr)$. The proof combines auxiliary prime factors with a mean square estimate for bilinear sums. We obtain the minor arc bound through harmonic switching and high moments, replacing arithmetic divisibility conditions by independent projective lines. We remove the auxiliary weights using Selberg's sieve.

items.title: Uniformization of topological MV-algebras
items.summary: In this paper, First, we prove that for every topological MV-algebra the topology is induced by a uniformity. As a application, we obtain that every topological MV-algebra is completely regular and every \(T_0\) first countable topological MV-algebra is metrizable. Second, we study the completion of the canonical difference uniformity in topological MV-algebra. Finally, we construct some examples show that not all topological MV-algebras are canonically completable and the property of canonically completable topological MV-algebra does not imply local order convexity.

items.title: An almost sharp tomas-stein restriction theorem for a class of anisotropic operators
items.summary: Let $d\geq 2$. For each $j\in \{1,\dots,d\}$, let ${\ell}_{j}\geq 1$ and $m_{j}\geq 2$ be integers, and let $a_{j}$ be a nonzero real number. We prove that the oscillatory integral operator \begin{equation*} T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f(x):=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}} e^{\dot{\imath} \left(a_{1}x^{{\ell}_{1}}_{1}y^{m_{1}}_{1}+\dots +a_{d}x^{{\ell}_{d}}_{d}y^{m_{d}}_{d} \right)}f(y)dy,\;\;\; x\in \mathbb{R}^{d}, \end{equation*} satisfies the restriction estimate \begin{equation*} \|T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})}\lesssim \|f\|_{L^{p}(\mathbb{R}^{d})}, \end{equation*} for each $1\leq p\leq 2$, whenever $(\frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}-\frac{1}{m_{j}}+1)\frac{2}{p^{\prime}}\geq 1$, for every $j\in Γ$, and \begin{equation*} \mathcal{E}:=\min{\left\{\min_{1\leq j\leq d}{\frac{m_{j}}{{\ell}_{j}}},\,\min_{1\leq k\leq d}{\frac{d-1}{\sum_{j\neq k} \frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}+\frac{2}{m_{k}}}}\right\}}> \frac{2}{p^{\prime}}. \end{equation*} We also give counterexamples that show that the condition $\mathcal{E}\geq 2/p^{\prime}$ is necessary for this restriction inequality.

items.title: VEM-bubble discretisation and iterative coupling algorithm for a fluid induced seismicity model with rate-and-state friction
items.summary: This work addresses the discretisation and iterative coupling algorithm for an induced seismicity model accounting for fault reactivation and slip driven by subsurface fluid injection. The model couples single-phase Darcy flow in both the porous matrix and the fault network with a quasi-static poroelastic mechanical response in the bulk and fault slip governed by a rate-and-state friction law with radiation damping stabilisation leading to a quas-dynamic formulation. The contact mechanics problem is discretised using the Virtual Element Method with bubble stabilisation of the facewise constant Lagrange multiplier. It is combined with a Hybrid Finite Volume scheme for the mixed-dimensional Darcy flow model. The time discretisation is implicit and the nonlinear system is solved at each time step using an iterative coupling algorithm which iterates between the Darcy flow, the frictional contact-mechanics, and the state differential equation. The contraction of this iterative coupling algorithm is established with a smallness assumption on the time step independent on the mesh size. This proves convergence of the fixed-point as well as well-posedness of the system. The frictional contact-mechanical model is solved using a semi-smooth Newton algorithm based on a local nonlinear inversion of the friction rate-and-state law and a block Gauss--Seidel preconditioner exploiting the structure of the VEM-bubble-$\mathbb{P}^0$ mixed discretisation.

items.title: Branch Obstructions for Area-Minimizing Currents and Flat Critical Points of Weakly-Conformal Maps
items.summary: We study two problems motivated by the local geometry of conformal $φ$-curves. First, let $T$ be a $k$-dimensional locally area-minimizing integral current in Euclidean space, with $k\geq3$, codimension at least two, no boundary, and a locally conformally flat induced metric on $\operatorname{reg} T$. We prove the following branch obstruction: at any rapid-decay branch point whose planar frequency differs from $2$, every nonzero cyclic component of every cylindrical normalized tangent function has repetition multiplicity at least two. Consequently, the nonintegral-frequency points of densities $2$ and $3$ in the rapid-decay branch set have Hausdorff dimension at most $k-3$. On the full branch set, they have zero $\mathcal H^{k-2}$ measure. These conclusions apply to Euclidean image currents of conformal $φ$-curves with locally conformally flat domains, provided the image currents satisfy the stated hypotheses. Second, for $C^j$ weakly-conformal maps between smooth Riemannian manifolds, with domain dimension $k\geq3$ and $j\geq2$, we prove that all derivatives of orders $1$ through $j$ vanish at every critical point. As a consequence, for smooth weakly-conformal maps with connected domain, we establish a curvature condition under which the map is constant or has no critical points. The flatness and continuation results apply in particular to conformal $φ$-curves with the corresponding regularity and curvature assumptions. Finally, we examine the Borůvka cone, which illustrates the role of regularity and the distinction between critical points and branch points.

items.title: The symmetric Gaussian isoperimetric problem in the plane
items.summary: We resolve the symmetric Gaussian isoperimetric conjecture in the plane: every minimizer of Gaussian perimeter among centrally symmetric sets of prescribed Gaussian measure is a centered ball, a symmetric strip, or the complement of one of these sets. A quadrant-reflection argument reduces the problem to unconditional sets. The planar structural results of Barchiesi, Cagnetti and Julin then leave only a noncircular strictly convex stationary oval. We exclude this oval by an explicit volume-preserving and perimeter-decreasing linear deformation, which geometrically corresponds to an "unconditional squeezing". More generally, without requiring any symmetry assumptions, we show that any noncircular closed embedded $λ$-self-shrinker is always unstable via linear deformations. We also record a reduction to the unconditional case in dimension three, using an orthogonal equipartition theorem of Musin.

items.title: A capillary logarithmic Gauss curvature flow and the capillary Minkowski problem
items.summary: We study a logarithmic Gauss curvature flow of strictly convex capillary hypersurfaces in the Euclidean half-space. For an acute contact angle and an arbitrary positive smooth prescribed function, we prove that a suitable initial dilation yields a global solution which converges smoothly after a horizontal translation with a uniquely determined constant velocity. As an application, we provide a logarithmic flow proof of the capillary Minkowski problem, previously established by Mei-Wang-Weng [Adv. Math. 469, 110230 (2025)].

items.title: Shifted Lagrangian geometry of curves in Radko surfaces
items.summary: We describe the shifted Lagrangian geometry of curves in Radko surfaces, through their global integrations and their homotopy Poisson algebras. We construct the adjoint symplectic groupoid of the surface explicitly, show that admissible curves integrate to embedded Lagrangian subgroupoids, which are 1-shifted Lagrangians, and characterize when their shifted intersections are clean. For a component of the degeneracy locus, a canonical Hamiltonian flow on its shifted self-intersection recovers the modular period. On the infinitesimal side, the homotopy Poisson algebra of a connected admissible curve not contained in the degeneracy locus is $L_\infty$-isomorphic to its underlying cochain complex, and its $L_\infty$-isomorphism class is determined by the total contact multiplicity. The brackets of arity at least two can be removed by a change of tubular neighbourhood exactly when all contacts are transverse. At tangential contacts, the binary bracket retains the modular vector field. We establish this distinction using a general characterization of the $L_\infty$-isomorphisms induced by changes of tubular neighbourhood, valid for arbitrary coisotropic submanifolds.

items.title: Exact local spectral thresholds for loose and tight Hamilton cycles in $3$-graphs
items.summary: For an $n$-vertex $3$-uniform hypergraph $H$, let $σ(H)$ denote the minimum adjacency spectral radius of its vertex links. We determine the exact thresholds for $σ(H)$ that force loose and tight Hamilton cycles for all sufficiently large admissible orders, and give constructions showing that each bound is best possible. The loose threshold is $(1+\sqrt{13})n/8+O(1)$, with two forms according to $n$ modulo four. The tight threshold is $2n/3+O(1)$, with four forms determined by $n$ modulo three and, when $3\mid n$, modulo nine. The resulting spectral conditions and the corresponding minimum vertex degree conditions do not imply one another. For loose cycles, we combine fractional packing stability and absorption with exact completion near a space barrier. For tight cycles, spectral stability and rooted sampling reduce the problem to three extremal configurations. We resolve these configurations by controlling the spectral loss caused by missing triples and constructing short paths that extend to Hamilton cycles, including in the presence of exceptional vertices.

items.title: A proof of the Theta conjecture
items.summary: We prove the touching refinement of the Theta conjecture of Interdonato and Iraci, giving a formula for $Θ_{e_\ell}Θ_{e_k}\nabla E_{d,j}$ as a weighted sum over parking functions with decorated rises and valleys and touch number $j$. Summing over $j$ gives the Theta conjecture. As corollaries, we prove the valley Delta conjecture of Haglund, Remmel, and Wilson and its generalized version proposed by Qiu and Wilson. Our proof compares algebraic and combinatorial recurrences using an extension of the plethystic substitution $X\mapsto(q-1)X$ to quasisymmetric functions. The algebraic recurrence follows from an endomorphism constructed by D'Adderio, Interdonato, Iraci and Pagaria on the Dyck path algebra of Carlsson and Mellit. The combinatorial recurrence is obtained by introducing signed labels and deleting the main diagonal. The two recurrences have the same initial conditions, which identifies the corresponding generating functions.

items.title: $λ_g$-Integrals on triple, one-part admissible covers
items.summary: We effectively compute all intersection numbers of the form $λ_gψ^d$ on moduli spaces of genus $g$ admissible covers with one point of full ramification and two additional branch points with arbitrary profile. We encode these invariants in appropriate generating functions, which we relate to the Hamiltonians of the KdV hierarchy.

items.title: Unique continuation property for $\bar\partial$ with $L^{2n}$ potentials
items.summary: We establish the sharp unique continuation property for the Cauchy--Riemann operator $\bar{\partial}$ in higher dimensions. Let $0\inΩ\subset \C^n$ be a domain. Suppose $u \in W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1,2}(Ω; \C^N)$ satisfies the differential inequality \[ |\bar{\partial} u| \leq V |u| \quad \text{a.e.~on } Ω \] with $V \in L_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2n}(Ω)$. If $u$ is $L^2$ flat at the origin, then $u \equiv 0$ on $Ω$.

items.title: Explicit expressions for iterates of power series
items.summary: We present several formulas for both the discrete and fractional iterates of an invertible power series $f,$ using a new unifying approach based on umbral calculus. Known formulas are extended, and their proofs simplified, while new expressions are introduced. In particular, by employing $q$-calculus identities, we eliminate the requirement for $f'(0)$ to equal $1$ and the resulting general expressions for the iterative logarithm are also obtained.

items.title: Total variation error bounds for Schrödinger-Föllmer samplers
items.summary: Sampling from high-dimensional, multimodal target distributions plays a fundamental role in scientific computing, statistics and machine learning. Recently, the Schrödinger-Föllmer sampler (SFS) has been proposed by Huang et al. (IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory, 2025) as an efficient sampling algorithm that transports the degenerate distribution at $t=0$ to the target distribution at $t=1$, without relying on long-time ergodicity. In this paper, we establish non-asymptotic error bounds for SFS in the total variation distance by deriving regularization estimates for the associated Kolmogorov equation via the Bismut-Elworthy-Li formula. When the drift can be computed exactly, a convergence rate of order $\mathcal{O}( h|\ln h|)$ was obtained under certain smoothness conditions on the drift with a uniform time step-size $h>0$. When the drift is approximated by Monte Carlo methods, we obtain a convergence rate of order $\mathcal{O}( h|\ln h|+ 1/M)$, where $M$ is the number of samples used in the Monte Carlo approximation. This yields a sharper dependence on $M$ than the existing bound $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{M})$ in the $L^2$-Wasserstein distance in the aforementioned paper, by turning the total variation error to the weak error analysis in the setting of non-smooth test functions. Numerical experiments are presented to illustrate the convergence rate with respect to the time step-size $h$ and the Monte Carlo sample size $M$ and the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

items.title: Finite-time Cholesky Factorization
items.summary: We propose an algorithm for estimating the Cholesky factorization of positive, semi-definite matrices without pivoting. Our method has the same data access pattern as the canonical Cholesky method, and therefore is amenable to familiar hardware optimization techniques. Our method interprets the factorization task as a variational problem and in turn solves it using an induced dynamical system. We study the rate of convergence of this dynamical system to its stationary state for both positive definite and semi-definite matrices. Numerical experiments validate that our method is competitive with pivoted Cholesky on several practical examples.

items.title: Sampling Colorings on $G(n, d/n)$ via Glauber Dynamics
items.summary: We study the mixing time of Glauber dynamics for sampling uniformly from the proper $q$-colorings of sparse Erdős-Rényi random graphs $G(n,d/n)$. Our main result establishes that with probability $1-o(1)$ over the draw of $G$, Glauber dynamics is rapidly mixing for every $q\geq d+d^{1/2+\varepsilon}$, given any fixed $0<\varepsilon\leq1/2$ and any sufficiently large fixed $d$. In particular, the surplus of colors above $d$ is sublinear and close to $\sqrt{d}$. The achieved color range therefore approaches the tree uniqueness threshold and improves over the previously best achievable number of colors $q > 1.763 d$ due to Efthymiou, Hayes, Stefankovic, and Vigoda [SODA 2018]. Moreover, our mixing-time bound is $O(n^{2+o_d(1)})$, and hence almost quadratic as $d\rightarrow\infty$. Our proof is based on establishing a spectral gap for block dynamics resulting from a suitable decomposition of $G(n,d/n)$ into blocks and singleton vertices, ensuring that every high-degree vertex is encapsulated within a block. Our main technical contribution is a novel way of establishing rapid mixing of block dynamics via an integrated Bochner-Bakry-Émery approach, which we expect to have applications beyond sampling colorings. We further devise a new block decomposition of $G(n,d/n)$ that strengthens and simplifies similar constructions used in previous work. Finally, to compare block and Glauber dynamics, we establish a novel recursive separator decomposition of tree-like blocks, together with a coupling argument that avoids the need for nearly uniform color marginals at vertices adjacent to hubs. This comparison argument might be of independent interest.

items.title: A Hadamard Formula for Equilibrium Envelopes under Parallel Deformation
items.summary: Let $(X,ω_0)$ be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension $n$, and let $U\Subset X$ have $C^{3,1}$ uniformly strongly pseudoconvex boundary. Consider the signed parallel family $U_t=\{ρ<t\}$, where $ρ$ is a defining function agreeing near $\partial U$ with the signed distance, negative in $U$. Let $u_t$ be the equilibrium envelope with zero obstacle on $X\setminus U_t$, and write $Σ_t=\partial U_t$, with outward unit normal $ν_t$. We prove that the normalized Monge--Ampère energy $e(t)=E_{ω_0}(u_t)$ belongs to $C^{1,1/2}([-τ,τ])$ for some $τ>0$ and satisfies the Hadamard formula $$ e'(t)=\frac{1}{n+1}\int_{Σ_t}\left(-\partial_{ν_t}u_t\right)^2 dσ_{ρ,t}^{\mathrm{tot}}, |t|<τ. $$ Here $dσ_{ρ,t}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the interior outward Anzellotti trace of $$ \frac{1}{V} d^cρ\wedge \sum_{p=0}^{n-1}(p+1) ω_{u_t}^{p}\wedgeω_0^{n-1-p}, V=\int_Xω_0^n, ω_{u_t}=ω_0+dd^c u_t. $$ This measure is positive and uniformly comparable to the induced surface measure. The proof combines uniform $C^{1,1}$ estimates up to the boundary from the interior with $1/2$-Hölder stability of the normal derivatives under the normal-flow identifications. We identify the boundary part of the normalized Monge--Ampère measure with the negative outward trace of a divergence-measure flux current. The one-sided weak-* limits of the mixed Bedford--Taylor boundary measures yield the weighted total flux appearing in the variation formula.

items.title: Nontrivial Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function and Its Derivative
items.summary: The nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie at the heart of analytic number theory. Through the explicit formulas, they govern the distribution of prime numbers: the closer all nontrivial zeros lie to the critical line $\Re(s)=\frac12$, the more uniformly the primes are distributed. The Riemann Hypothesis-asserting that all nontrivial zeros satisfy $\Re(s)=\frac12$-is equivalent to the optimal error bound $O(\sqrt{x}\log x)$ in the Prime Number Theorem. Beyond number theory, the zeros of $ζ(s)$ and its derivative $ζ'(s)$ are deeply intertwined: the horizontal distribution of $ζ'$-zeros near the critical line encodes information about the spacing of consecutive $ζ$-zeros. This paper establishes some results concerning the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function.

items.title: Geometric folding and maximal asymptotic variance
items.summary: Based on the recent breakthroughs by OpenAI and consequently by Binder-Ivrii-Prause-Smirnov, we develop a finite-scale folding method for the nonlinearity of a schlicht function, based on a signed critical-point count for superharmonic potentials and a quantitative target cutoff. Furthermore, we use a cylindrical root transform to reduce the logarithmic cost of access to the point at infinity. Combined with a Littlewood-Paley formula as well as dilation, the method yields the maximal asymptotic variance bound $Σ_{\max}^2\le1$ for the unrestricted schlicht class of normalized univalent functions.

items.title: Physics-informed neural networks in the small-data regime: A controlled comparison with classical PDE surrogates
items.summary: Neural surrogates for engineering models are often trained on large collections of simulated solutions. We investigate whether physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) can achieve accurate predictions from scarce labelled observations by incorporating governing equations and prescribed initial and boundary conditions. We introduce hierarchical loss weighting (H-PINN) and its gradient-direction-aware extension (HO-PINN), which adjust the emphasis on physical constraints according to higher-priority losses. Hierarchical PINNs are compared with Vanilla PINN, tuned gradient boosting, support-vector regression, and Gaussian-process regression on a heat equation and three heterogeneous two-phase-flow benchmarks. Experiments use 20--1000 labelled states and ten paired seeds. Each label is one coordinate--state observation, not a complete simulation. At least one PINN variant achieves the highest mean primary-target \(R^2\) in each interpolation and equation-assisted forecasting comparison at 20 and 50 labels. The advantage for water saturation persists across all tested budgets. Hierarchical weighting reduces variability across runs in selected settings. These results demonstrate that known physics can support accurate neural surrogate predictions from very few solution observations, at substantially higher fitting cost than the tested classical regressors.

items.title: Positive solutions of power equations in planar corner domains
items.summary: We study positive solutions of $Δu=λu^k$ on bounded planar corner domains with zero boundary values away from the vertex. For negative-power absorption we identify the admissible interval of Martin masses and prove uniqueness at the minimum mass. Along the ordinary boundary, we identify the weak Hessian endpoint and its sharp tail when the set of zero inward derivative has positive length. For superlinear sources we prove attainment of the largest positive Martin mass in the subcritical range. At criticality we construct a family of singular solutions with zero Martin mass and distinguish its members by their second logarithmic coefficient and the endpoint integrability of their Hessian differences. Above criticality an angular eigenvalue governs the Morse index away from its zero threshold. We also give sharp physical-Hessian asymptotics for finite-mass remainders and joint corner and side estimates for negative-power sources.

items.title: Strong error bounds at low regularity for a time approximation of the stochastic KdV equation driven by small additive noise
items.summary: We study strong temporal approximation of periodic stochastic Korteweg--de Vries equation driven by small additive \(Q\)-Wiener noise of amplitude \(\mathcal O(\varepsilon)\), \(0<\varepsilon\ll1\) under $H^s$-regularity, $s=1,2$. This is a challenging problem, due to the additional derivative term in the nonlinearity and the lack of suitable exponential moment bounds for the exact solutions. Exploiting the small-noise regime, we first decompose the solution into a deterministic KdV flow and a stochastic component; then we linearize the obtained stochastic equation and approximate the resulting equation by means of Fourier analytic techniques. Combining the small-noise linearization error, the discretization error of the linearized equation, and the deterministic temporal approximation error, and assuming suitable conditions on the deterministic solver, we get strong errors of size $\mathcal{O}(τ+\varepsilon^2)$ under \(H^1\)-regularity and of size $\mathcal{O}(τ^2+\varepsilon^2)$ under $H^2$-regularity. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first strong error bounds achieved for numerical time approximations of the stochastic KdV at low regularity.

items.title: Holomorphic integer-graded vertex operator superalgebras are purely even
items.summary: We prove that a simple, self-contragredient, rational, $C_2$-cofinite, integer-graded holomorphic vertex operator superalgebra of CFT-type has zero odd part. We first show that a hypothetical nonzero odd part would be a simple current of categorical dimension $-1$ over a strongly rational pointed VOA with four simple modules. We then prove that every nonvacuum simple current of a strongly rational VOA has strictly positive lowest conformal weight. This leads to a contradiction with Dong-Jiao-Xu's theorem on the positivity of categorical dimension.

items.title: Special Lagrangian cones in Deep Learning
items.summary: We introduce a matrix generalization of the cone of Harvey and Lawson and prove that it is an exact special Lagrangian manifold. We further show that it belongs to a family of exact special Lagrangian manifolds that foliate the balanced manifold arising in deep learning.

items.title: Derivations tangent to polar discriminants
items.summary: We describe the module of logarithmic derivations along the discriminant of a stable polar representation of a reductive algebraic group. It splits into derivations along the fibres of the quotient map and a free summand lifted from logarithmic derivations along the associated branch divisor. This gives a uniform extension of previous results on full adjoint discriminants. We prove that, for visible stable polar actions of semisimple groups with finite generic stabilizer, the discriminant is a free divisor. For stable periodic gradings of arbitrary order with semisimple degree-zero group, we construct explicit Saito matrices from the infinitesimal action and the gradients of basic invariants, which yields determinantal equations for several exceptional discriminants. In particular, starting with exceptional Lie algebras, we provide examples of free discriminants of degrees 60, 120, 126 and 240 for inner gradings and a degree-72 example for an outer one.

items.title: Singularities in leaf closures on complex surfaces
items.summary: We prove a geometric and dynamical criterion excluding minimal sets contained in the regular locus of a holomorphic foliation on a compact complex surface. In particular, we prove that every Jouanolou foliation of degree at least two has no exceptional minimal set. We also give an explicit lower bound, growing linearly with the degree, for the number of singularities in every regular leaf closure of a Jouanolou foliation. This bound persists under small perturbations, as does the existence of a nonempty open saturated set whose leaves accumulate at all singularities. Under finite pullback unramified over the singular set, the bound is multiplied by the degree of the normalised component over the base leaf. Together with a general persistence theorem, this yields nonempty analytic open sets of foliations on every smooth projective surface with arbitrarily large uniform lower bounds on the number of singularities in their regular leaf closures. On double-plane K3 surfaces, we obtain foliations with ample canonical bundle and explicitly describe and count their singularities.

items.title: Variational Properties and KL Exponent of Square-Transformed Polyhedral Composite Optimization
items.summary: We consider one of the most common reparameterization techniques, the square transformation. Assuming the original objective function is the sum of a smooth function and a polyhedral function, we study the variational properties of the objective function after reparameterization. In particular, we first study the minimal norm of the subdifferential of the reparameterized objective function. Second, we compute the second subderivative of the reparameterized objective function on a linear subspace, which allows us to fully characterize the subclass of stationary points of the reparameterized objective function that correspond to stationary points of the original objective function. Finally, utilizing the representation of the minimal norm of the subdifferential, we show that the Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz (KL) exponent of the reparameterized function can be deduced from that of the original function. Applications to concrete optimization models are discussed.

items.title: Stationary Mean-Field singular control of an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process
items.summary: Motivated by continuous-time optimal inventory management, we study a class of stationary mean-field control problems with singular controls. The dynamics are modeled by a mean-reverting Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, and the performance criterion is given by a quadratic long-time average expected cost functional. The mean-field dependence is through the stationary mean of the controlled process itself, which enters the ergodic cost functional. We relate optimal controls for the stationary mean-field control problem to equilibria of an associated stationary mean-field game. In particular, optimal controls induce equilibria of the associated game, while the converse holds true within the class of admissible controls satisfying an additional integrability requirement. Finally, we solve the stationary mean-field game explicitly, thereby obtaining an explicitly characterized optimal reflection policy for the stationary mean-field control problem within this restricted class.

items.title: Linear disjointness and values of Mahler M-functions
items.summary: We prove that the algebra generated by the values of Mahler M-functions at algebraic points admits a decomposition as the tensor product, over Q, of a countable family of linearly disjoint algebras. Consequently, the study of linear and algebraic relations among such values reduces to the corresponding problem within each of these smaller algebras. Our proof relies on recent advances of the authors on Mahler's method in several variables. As an application, we obtain a complete description of the algebraic relations among the values of the Fredholm series and their derivatives at nonzero algebraic points. This fully resolves an old problem originating in Mahler's work.

items.title: Orbits along primes in totally minimal systems
items.summary: In this paper, we show that every totally minimal system admits a point whose orbit along the primes is dense. Moreover, assuming the Dickson-Hardy-Littlewood conjecture, we show that in any totally minimal distal system, the orbit along the primes of every point is dense.

items.title: On the gradient conjecture at infinity: Finite spherical length for gradient trajectories of definable potentials
items.summary: We prove that for every open $U \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ the spherical projection of every gradient trajectory $θ(t)$, $t \geq 0$, of a definable $C^1$-potential $F \colon U \to \mathbb{R}$ has finite length and, in particular, converges (directional convergence). In other words, every gradient trajectory of a definable $C^1$-potential has finite total angular motion. Here, definable means definable in an arbitrary o-minimal structure expanding the real field. Notably, the gradient trajectory in this result is an arbitrary solution of the gradient flow differential equation (whose solutions may not be unique) with no further assumptions: The gradient trajectory may be unbounded and diverge to infinity or it may be convergent. The established theorem therefore provides affirmative answers to both the gradient conjecture at infinity for definable potentials and the definable Thom gradient conjecture. We extend our conclusions from the Euclidean metric to a general class of ambient metrics including Riemannian metrics and we establish uniform local upper bounds for the lengths of the spherical projections of gradient flow trajectories. We finally apply our findings to the training of deep neural networks (DNNs) to conclude that, in the case of definable and continuously differentiable activation and loss functions, the spherical projection of the DNN training flow must always converge (directional convergence).

items.title: Function spaces, web spaces, and Lawson-compactness in Domain Theory
items.summary: This paper investigates the structural properties of function spaces and their connections with Lawson-compactness and web spaces in domain theory. First, using finite-refinement and palette methods, we characterize the topological spaces $X$ for which the function space $[X\to L]$ is an RB-domain for every RB-domain $L$. In particular, we establish the equivalence between this preservation property and the condition that $X$ is compact, core compact, core coherent, and a web space. We further investigate its relationship with RW$^*$-spaces and obtain partial results concerning the Lawson-Mislove's problem. Second, we construct a countably based topological space $Z$ that is compact, core compact, core coherent, and a web space, but is neither a wide web space nor a C-space. More precisely, its lattice of open sets is a continuous frame satisfying $κ$-distributivity for every finite cardinal $κ\geq 2$, while failing to be $ω$-distributive. This provides a negative answer to a question raised by Erne and demonstrates that finite distributivity, even at every finite level, does not imply countable distributivity. Finally, by introducing labelled posets and employing constructions based on presheaves over finite sets and their element posets, we prove that every Lawson-compact domain is a Scott-continuous retract of a Lawson-compact algebraic domain, thereby answering a problem proposed by Kou. As applications, we show that the function space from an RB-domain to a Lawson-compact domain is Lawson-compact. Moreover, for an FS-domain $X$, we establish that $X$ is an RB-domain if and only if $[X\to L]$ is Lawson-compact for every Lawson-compact domain $L$. This characterization also yields the existence of an FS-domain $X$ and a Lawson-compact algebraic domain $L$ for which $[X\to L]$ is not continuous. This gives a negative answer to the question raised by Shen et al.

items.title: The permutation automorphism groups of irreducible cyclic codes
items.summary: The study of permutation automorphism groups of cyclic codes is a central topic in algebraic coding theory. A cyclic code over $\mathbb{F}_q$ is called irreducible if its check polynomial is irreducible over $\mathbb{F}_q$, and it is non-degenerate if it is not periodic. Such a non-degenerate code is standard if its permutation automorphism group is equal to the group generated by the cyclic shift and the Frobenius automorphism, and non-standard otherwise. In this paper, we give a complete classification of all non-standard non-degenerate irreducible cyclic codes, using the classification of finite simple groups. Our result shows that, apart from a small number of explicit exceptional families and their descendants under certain secondary constructions, every non-degenerate irreducible cyclic code is standard, and up to four explicit exceptions, every nonzero degenerate cyclic code is non-standard. This classification has several consequences. First, it yields a general description of non-standard linear recurring sequence subgroups, extending the earlier work of Brison and Nogueira; secondly, it establishes the Schmidt-White conjecture for all non-standard non-degenerate irreducible cyclic codes. Moreover, our results provide strong evidence in support of the conjecture of Berger and Charpin that almost all cyclic codes are standard.

items.title: A Llarull type theorem on complete noncompact manifolds
items.summary: Let $n\geq3$, $2\leq k\leq n-1$, and $m=n-k-1$. We prove that a complete, connected, noncompact, oriented manifold $(M^n,g)$ with scalar curvature $R_M\geq k(k-1)$ is isometric to $\mathbb{S}^k\times\mathbb{T}^m_Λ\times\mathbb{R}$ if it admits a smooth proper map of non-zero degree to $\mathbb{S}^k\times\mathbb{T}^m\times\mathbb{R}$ whose spherical component is 1-Lipschitz. We also establish a weighted scalar curvature obstruction at infinity for sphere-torus targets with a higher dimensional Euclidean factor under suitable control of the Euclidean component. These results hold in all dimensions without a spin assumption.

items.title: Lipschitz inner rates of normal surface singularities
items.summary: In this article, we connect the local Lipschitz geometry of a normal surface singularity with a rational homology sphere link to the analytic semigroup $S_{an}(\tilde{X})$ associated with a convenient resolution. Under certain restriction, we provide an explicit computational characterization of the Lipschitz rate $q_v$ associated with an irreducible exceptional curve $E_v$ in terms of the semigroup. We also show that removing the restriction we get examples when $q_v$ cannot be determined from the semigroup. Interestingly enough, this phenomenon already happens for rational singularities. Indeed, we exemplify that the inner rates of rational singularities are not topological.

items.title: Vector metrics with values in pre-Riesz spaces I: transfer of order convergence along vector lattice covers
items.summary: Vector metric spaces in the sense of Çevik and Altun take values in a vector lattice, but their axioms use only the order of the value space. We develop the theory for vector metrics with values in an Archimedean pre-Riesz space $E$, i.e.\ an ordered vector space admitting a bipositive order dense embedding $i$ into a vector lattice $Y$. We ask when an $E$-valued vector metric $d$ and the vector-lattice-valued metric $i\circ d$ have the same convergent and Cauchy nets and sequences. Relatively uniform convergence transfers along every cover. For nets, $\mathrm{o}_3$-convergence transfers if and only if the cover has an intrinsic domination property. This property holds for pervasive covers, by a result of Kalauch and van Gaans, for uniformly dense covers and in finite dimensions; it fails for an example of Kalauch and van Gaans. Sequential convergence transfers under a countable domination property implied by uniform density, but not under pervasiveness. For uncountable $Γ$, the vector lattice $\mathbb{R}\mathbf 1\oplus c_{00}(Γ)$ is pervasive in its Dedekind completion $\ell^\infty(Γ)$ without the transfer, while for countable $Γ$ the transfer holds; the difference is explained by order separability. In finite dimensions, with a closed generating cone, all these convergences coincide with norm convergence in every cover. For $C^1[0,1]$-valued integral metrics, positivity of the kernel on the diagonal forces all order convergences to coincide with $L^1$-convergence. For the Volterra kernel $(t-s)_+$, by contrast, $L^1$-convergence, relatively uniform convergence and order convergence are pairwise different, and we describe each explicitly.

items.title: Reconstructing Flash-Evoked Potentials in the Human Brain and Tracking Cortical Activity Using Spatiotemporal Filtering: Numerical Simulation Study
items.summary: Electroencephalographic source reconstruction of visual evoked activity is challenging because distributed, temporally evolving, and overlapping cortical sources generate scalp potentials. We present a controlled simulation framework for flash visual evoked potentials (FVEPs) based on a coupled Jansen--Rit neural mass network and a realistic finite-element EEG forward model. The framework generates a sequential activation pattern across early visual, parietal, and frontal regions and enables direct comparison of reconstructed activity with known ground truth. Standardized Kalman filtering (SKF), change-rate SKF (CrSKF), conventional Kalman filtering (KF), and linearly constrained minimum variance (LCMV) beamforming are compared using parcel-wise time courses, temporal lags, and assessments of spatial focality and Earth Mover's Distance. In the inverse comparison, SKF and CrSKF preserve the principal temporal progression more consistently than KF and LCMV, while CrSKF produces smoother temporal estimates. The results also demonstrate parcel-wise leakage and reduced separation of closely spaced components, emphasizing the need to interpret temporal ordering together with spatial reconstruction quality. The proposed framework provides a reproducible test environment for evaluating dynamic EEG inverse methods under controlled noise conditions.

items.title: Completions of vector metric spaces and the diagonal property of order convergence
items.summary: A vector metric space carries a distance with values in an ordered vector space $E$; a sequence converges if its distances to the limit are dominated by a sequence decreasing to zero in $E$. We show that, for Archimedean $E$, every $E$-valued vector metric space has a completion if and only if order Cauchy sequences in $E$ converge and $E$ has the diagonal property of order convergence (SDP): for every double sequence $(a^k_n)$ with $a^k_n\downarrow_n0$ there are indices $n_k$ and $e_k\downarrow 0$ with $a^k_{n_k}\le e_k$. In vector lattices this is the classical diagonal property of Kantorovich, equivalently the strong Egoroff property. We show that its standard characterisations remain valid in Archimedean ordered vector spaces, and that it holds if and only if convergence in every $E$-valued vector metric space satisfies the iterated limit axiom. For an ordered Banach space with a closed normal cone, all completions exist if and only if the norm is $σ$-order continuous; if the cone has an interior point, all vector metrics are then scalar. By a theorem of Veksler and of Hager and van Mill, for compact Hausdorff $K$ either $K$ is an almost $P$-space and $C(K)$-valued vector metrics are scalar, or there are countable $C(K)$-valued vector metric spaces without completion. A product of ordered vector spaces with (SDP) and nonzero cones has (SDP) if and only if there are fewer than $\mathfrak b$ factors, extending a result of Hager and van Mill for $\mathbb{R}^A$. We also prove permanence results for direct summands and uniformly dense vector lattice covers of pre-Riesz spaces.

items.title: Calligraphs and sphere realizations
items.summary: We introduce a recursive procedure for computing the number of realizations of a minimally rigid graph on the sphere up to rotations. We accomplish this by combining two ingredients. The first is a framework that allows us to think of such realizations as of elements of a moduli space of stable rational curves with marked points. The second is the idea of splitting a minimally rigid graph into two subgraphs, called calligraphs, that admit one degree of freedom and that share only a single edge and a further vertex. This idea has been recently employed for realizations of graphs in the plane up to isometries. The key result is that we can associate to a calligraph a triple of natural numbers with a special property: whenever a minimally rigid graph is split into two calligraphs, the number of realizations of the former equals the product of the two triples of the latter, where this product is specified by a fixed quadratic form. These triples and quadratic form codify the fact that we express realizations as intersections of two curves on the blowup of a sphere along two pairs of complex conjugate points.

items.title: Splitting-strategies for arbitrary-order fully mixed finite element discretizations of the Biot equations
items.summary: We study the fully-mixed formulation of the Biot equations which is characterized by a symmetric coupling between flow and deformation while each subphysics has internally a saddle point structure. This enables the use of stable mixed finite elements for each subproblem without a strong compatibility condition across the two subphysics. To exploit this flexibility while preserving the conservation structure of both subproblems, we consider fully mixed finite element methods in which the symmetry of the elastic stress tensor is enforced weakly, often referred to as a five-field formulation. The resulting mixed formulation exhibits an overarching saddle-point structure whose stability is determined by suitable inf-sup conditions. Inf-sup stability is established for several families of discrete spaces of arbitrary order, leading to optimal a priori error estimates. Iterative splitting strategies following the classical fixed-stress split with additional tuning are specifically investigated for the fully mixed formulation with proof of convergence and rates depending on the coupling strength. Contrary to previous analyses on coupled problems with a symmetric structure, we theoretically prove the efficacy of negative stabilization, consistent with Schur-complement ideas. Numerical results based on analytical solutions and the classical 2D Mandel problem and a 3D footing problem are presented supporting the theory.

items.title: Law-Invariant Operators for Stochastic Mechanics
items.summary: A central objective in stochastic mechanics is to separate deterministic physical behavior from the probability laws governing uncertain inputs. While classical spectral approaches achieve this separation in linear settings, nonlinear responses introduce interactions beyond conventional second-order variability response functions (VRF). Inspired by the spirit of VRFs, this work establishes that, for a fixed physical system, uncertainty propagation is described by a law-invariant operator mapping input realizations to responses, governed by the underlying physics and the deterministic parameters of the system. Different probability laws affect the input sampling and resulting response statistics, but not the mapping operator. We establish this law invariance under complete, invertible coordinate transformations and develop complementary, Fourier, fixed-reference polynomial-chaos (PCE) and finite element method (FEM) transfer formulations. Fourier captures nonlinear cross-frequency interactions and recovers the classical VRF in the appropriate linear limit, PCE describes coupling among stochastic modes, while FEM expresses the deterministic inverse-stiffness action. Neural approximations of these deterministic operators are investigated through analytical and finite-element benchmarks, examining cross-law generalization, the influence of training distributions and stochastic excitation, and the prediction of response fields and statistics. The results demonstrate the potential for reusing learned physical operators across different stochastic laws without retraining, while highlighting the importance of adequate training coverage and the challenges of accurately estimating low-probability events.

items.title: Avoiding short progressions in Euclidean Ramsey theory II
items.summary:
Recently, Currier, Moore, and Yip developed a general framework for constructing colorings avoiding prescribed monochromatic arithmetic progressions in Euclidean Ramsey theory. Writing $\ell_m$ for an $m$-term arithmetic progression with unit spacing, they proved $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,\ell_{20})$ and $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,α\ell_{6889})$ for every $α>0$. We refine and simplify their framework, proving $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,α\ell_{22})$ for every $α>0$. We further establish $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,α\ell_{21})$ except possibly for four values of $α^2$, and $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,α\ell_{17})$ for all but finitely many $α>0$. Our approach also recovers several earlier results and avoids some technical arguments used in previous works.

items.title: Induced packing treewidth III. Branch decompositions
